News.title: Huge wildfire erupts in Brit holiday hotspot Costa del Sol with 5 helicopters battling inferno & emergency alert issued
News.content:
A MASSIVE wildfire has broken out by a Spanish village popular with Brit expats, sparking a level one emergency.

At least five helicopters and over 60 firefighters have raced to the inferno near Costa del Sol and are furiously battling the flames.



The raging blaze is believed to have been sparked inside a small Catholic chapel at around 3pm.

Dramatic photos show fiery red flames scorching treetops as a monstrous wall of thick smoke blankets the region.



The wildfire ripped through the hillsides close to the mountain village of Benahavis, a short drive away from Marbella.

Emergency text messages have pinged across the region as anxious locals strive to escape unharmed from the fires.

Residents have been urged to hunker down in their homes and shut all doors and windows as choking smoke spirals through the air.

Andalucia’s Acting Minister for Health said: “If you are in the area, shelter inside a masonry house or building.

“Close doors and windows. Follow the instructions from 1-1-2 and the emergency services. Avoid risks.”

It comes just months after deadly wildfires devastated the hillsides of Almeria, killing 15.



Nine Brits were among the victims of the monster blaze on July 9.

News.title: Hayden Panettiere’s boyfriend Brian Hickerson ‘screams about her death as he & brother cuffed by cops after bar brawl’
News.content:
HAYDEN Panettiere’s on-off boyfriend Brian Hickerson was cuffed by cops last night after an alleged incident at a bar.

According to sources, the 37-year-old actor started yelling at officers about her death while cuffed and sitting on the sidewalk.



Brian had allegedly been drinking for hours with his brother Zach at the Wild Wing Cafe bar in Greenville, South Carolina, on Saturday night before the pair were thrown out over a chair tossing incident, TMZ reports.

Sources told the outlet that the outing took a turn when Brian went up to the bar to talk to fellow patrons before allegedly picking up a stool and throwing it behind him.



Video obtained by TMZ shows Brian being raised into the air by someone during an argument before being carried out of the bar while a bartender yells “Let him go!”

The Greenville Police Department told the outlet that they were called to the bar about an alleged assault and found the two brothers in an argument with others outside.

read more on Hayden Panettiere SAFETY FEARS Hayden Panettiere ‘hired security to keep Brian away from her’ in last months

Both men were put in cuffs but only Zach was arrested for disorderly conduct after launching into a profanity-filled tirade.

Brian was released by cops but not before accusing the police department of leaking information about Hayden’s death.

“GPD leaked it when my girlfriend died,” he yelled after officers put him in cuffs, per TMZ.

Last month, the Heroes and Nashville star was found unresponsive at her Greenville apartment where she had been staying with Brian.



According to a police report obtained by The U.S. Sun, Zach entered the apartment to discover the actress unresponsive in a chair. (Brian was sleeping in another room of the apartment.)

Zach told TMZ that Brian administered Narcan to the 36-year-old mom-of-two who was nominated for two Golden Globes, but she was pronounced dead at the scene.

According to 911 dispatch audio, she was suffering from a cardiac arrest and suspected overdose.

Hayden’s exact cause of death remains unknown

An investigation into her death has been launched by the Drug Enforcement Administration.



Meanwhile, a criminal investigation has reportedly been launched to find out if anyone was responsible for her death.

Just three months before her death, the actress had whippets and booze delivered to her Nashville hotel room, according to Page Six.

This was at the same time she was claiming to be sober and healthy while promoting her book after suffering from alcoholism and addiction for years.

Following Hayden’s tragic death, her mother Lesley Vogel slammed her daughter’s rekindled relationship with Brian, revealing that the family were desperate to “get rid” of him.

The pair began dating in 2018 and the following year after the family already raised concerns about the relationship, Brian was arrested for domestic violence after an incident at Hayden’s home.



The actress allegedly sustained injuries to her arms, ears, and neck area.

But just a few days after his arrest, they were spotted holding hands while shopping for new cars despite him being hit with a felony charge which was later dismissed in part due to no cooperating witnesses.

On Valentine’s Day 2020, Brian was arrested again for domestic violence while the pair was vacationing in Wyoming and he was sentenced to 45 days in jail. According to reports, he served 12 days in jail.



Despite Hayden releasing a statement about the abusive nature of the relationship, the pair were seen together again in July 2021, shortly before Brian was accused of getting into a massive group brawl in Hollywood.

They were seen again in 2023 at her brother Jansen’s funeral and Brian helped her through an LA airport while she was on crutches in March of this year.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

According to TMZ, the couple were fully together and hiding their rekindled romance.

“Hayden’s team felt Brian was bad for business,” a source told the outlet.

News.title: Moment Ukraine naval drone ‘destroys unmanned Russian boat’ in ‘first-ever’ drone battle at sea
News.content:
THIS is the dramatic moment Ukraine destroys a Russian boat in the “first ever” battle between sea drones.

Multiple rounds of machine-gun fire blast into the hull of the unmanned Russian drone in newly released footage fromUkraine‘s navy.



After a volley of strikes, the bot submerges beneath the waves in a huge shower of water and thick, grey smoke.

Writing on Telegram yesterday, the Ukrainian navy called the mid-sea clash the “first-ever” battle between sea drones.



“This marks the first-ever naval engagement between uncrewed surface vessels”, the statement said.

Filmed aboard a Ukrainian Sargan 3000 USV vessel, the footage shows an M2 Browning .50 machine gun take aim.

It then fires across the sea, striking and sinking Putin’s sea drone as empty cartridges tumble from the weapon.

Bristling with heavy machine guns, unmanned sea bots can destroy vessels at distances of 2,000 yards and fire between 450–575 rounds per minute.

Intelligence gathered by Ukraine’s Main Intelligence Directorate detetcted the Russian target – and then fed the information back to the unmanned vessel

It is unclear precisely when the dramatic sea clash took place.



Deadly drone swarms unleashed by Ukraine have pushed back Vladimir Putin‘s armies – and are changing the scarred face of warfare forever.

Just days ago Ukraine hammered Siberian gas plants – which are 2,000 miles from the border – in its deepest strike into Russia to date.

The relentless attacks on fuel hubs is shattering Russia’s economy – and has left furious citizens brawling over petrol.



Volodymr Zelensky has spurred his forces into buidling some of the world’s most high-tech drones – with the latest invention dubbed “The Sun”.

The deadly new drone is creating a vast “kill zone” across the front line – pushing the battlefield towards a stalemate.

It can fly up to 190mph – and boasts an almost 100 per cent kill rate.

And in August, British-made drones struck Russia for the first time, killing at least six people in the biggest air raid on Moscow in two years.

More than 800 flying bots swarmed through the skies and rained hell down on Russia warehouses and factories.



Drone warfare has become a defining feature of the Ukraine-Russia war.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They are everywhere and do everything, from sinking ships to hauling half-dead soldiers off the battlefield.

Experts believe they are the new “kings of war” with defence ministries across the world pouring more cash into developing the deadly bots.

News.title: Nato jet scrambled over ‘drone sighting’ as emergency phone alert issued and airport closed in Lithuania
News.content:
SECURITY ALERT Nato jet scrambled over ‘drone sighting’ as emergency phone alert issued and airport closed in Lithuania

A NATO jet was scrambled after a flock of birds believed to be a drone was sighted over Vilnius airport.

The sighting sparked an immediate shutdown of Lithuania‘s primary travel hub and at least one fighter jet was dispatched in response.



After 38 minutes, the alert was lifted and the airport reopened after the jet got a closer look at the “threat”.

Lithuania’s National Crisis Management Centre said: “On initial radar readings, marks left by birds and drones can be similar.”



The jet was summoned from Siauliai in northern Lithuania.

The base is currently being used by the Italian air force as part of the Nato Baltic Air Defence mission.

Military drones have strayed into Finland, Romania, Estonia and Lithuania, stoking fear that the Ukraine war is spilling into Nato territory.

Russia has been accused of ramping up hybrid attacks on European nations it believes to be helping Kyiv.

Dozens of mysterious drones have been spotted in recent months as Putin’s urge to sow chaos among Nato nations continues.

The alliance scrambled fighter jets over Estonia after several drones were spotted in the Baltic nation’s airspace earlier this month.



The terrifying drone warning was issued in eight Estonian counties – as Turkish Nato planes were deployed to the scene.

Another alert was activated in Latvia along its border with Russia amid the chaos.

Colonel Uku Arold, Estonian Defence Forces’ spokesman, said: “There have been drones moving parallel to the eastern borders of both Estonia and Latvia.



“They entered Estonia which is why we activated the alarm.”

Over this weekend, a giant ammunition storage site burst into flames in Bulgaria, with Russia the prime suspect in the attack.

Secondary explosions were reported as flames were “moving from warehouse to warehouse,” said Gabrovo regional governor Kristina Sidorova.

Opposition MP Ivaylo Mirchev, co-leader of the pro-Western Yes, Bulgaria! party, linked the fire directly to Russia’s alleged hybrid sabotage campaign across Europe.

He said: “A few days ago we warned parliament that what Russia is doing in Leipzig is also happening in Bulgaria,” referring to a bomb-laden drone found at a German airport, which has been linked to Putin’s spooks.



It came as Putin – who once claimed he had no aggressive intentions against Ukraine – said he had no plan to invade or threaten existing Nato states in Europe.

He claimed: “There is no such threat, and there has never been.

“We are not threatening European countries, nor are we going to threaten them. Why would we?

“No one seems to even consider that we have no grounds for any conflict with Europe.”

Lithuania, where today’s false alarm was raised, has been in the sights of Putin’s cronies.



Kremlin firebrand Dmitry Medvedev threatened to reduce the Nato member and former Soviet state to “scorched earth” and wipe it “off the map”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His warning came after the Baltic state said it was negotiating with Washington over the possible deployment of US nuclear weapons in the country.

It comes as Putin has now increased the number of nuclear warheads deployed to a nine-year high, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI).

News.title: Should political party donations be capped? VOTE NOW
News.content:
POLL OF THE DAY Should political party donations be capped? VOTE NOW

NIGEL Farage recently secured donations totalling to £72million from two crypto billionaires to help give Reform a “fair fight” in the polls.

However, Angela Rayner has warned the Reform party leader he may have to hand back some of the money as the donations could be deemed unlawful.



Reform received two donations, each worth £36 million, from Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne in recent days – the largest single donation to a British political party in history.

The upcoming Rycroft Review says that overseas voters moving to the UK would be stopped from giving more than £100,000 in donations for a year after their arrival.



Farage’s two donors are British citizens, with Delo moving back to the UK from Hong Kong within the past year.

Ms Rayner insists that despite the review’s publish date sitting at the end of March, the findings will be backdated.



But Reform UK’s Robert Jenrick said the cash will allow the party to be “battle ready” and insisted the donations were legal.

News.title: Boris Johnson and European officials caught up in Ukraine train panic after Russian drone strike near Polish border
News.content:
BORIS Johnson was caught up in an incident at the Polish border after a Russian drone struck train tracks.

The former Prime Minister, who is understood to be unharmed, was travelling back from a security conference in Kyiv.



Panicked passengers were woken up at 5am as Mr Johnson’s train was temporarily evacuated because of nearby drone attacks, according to German outlet Der Spiegel.

Former Swedish premier and foreign minister Carl Bildt, who was on the same train as Johnson, said the train immediately after theirs was hit by the drone.



The “special train” received an “evacuation warning” but managed to escape across the border to Nato territory in Poland.

Bildt said: “This wasn’t our train [that was hit], but the one just minutes after us by the [Polish] border crossing.

“It was evacuated as the [Russian] drone approached and no one was hurt. Very good safety system.

“Our train just had an evacuation warning but could proceed to Dorohusk.

“The [Russian] attacks against [Ukraine] are intensifying.”

The incident came after another train on the Kyiv-Warsaw route was struck by a Russian drone just one mile from the Polish border.



The train was carrying 206 passengers who were seen running in fear after the attack.

No one was injured, according to Ukrainian railway authorities.

Shocking images show a huge fireball engulfing train tracks and flames lighting up the night sky.



Also on Mr Johnson’s train was Günter Sautter, Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s foreign and security-policy adviser.

There is no indication that their train was struck by a drone.

Johnson and other prominent Western figures had been attending the 2026 annual meeting of the Yalta European Strategy (YES) in Kyiv.

Russian independent news outlet Agentsvo reported: “A day after Putin threatened Europe with war, Russia struck the Kyiv–Warsaw train.

“The strike affected a special train carrying European politicians and diplomats.”



The attack comes days after US envoys visited Kyiv and Moscow hoping to revive Washington-led talks on ending Europe’s worst conflict since World War II, without securing a breakthrough.

Nato member Poland said a second drone struck near a border crossing, prompting Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski to accuse Putin of “escalating” the conflict.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Moscow struck the train “deliberately”.

He also accused Russia of attacking rail and energy infrastructure, as well as civilian buildings across the country, including in the west.

Zelensky said: “It is precisely to prevent these strikes from spreading further into Europe that Ukrainian men and women fight every day, give their lives, and do not allow the aggression to expand.



With Ukrainian airspace closed, trains to neighbouring Poland have been one of the main routes out of the war-torn country, often carrying refugees and packed with women and children.

Neither country reported casualties and Intercity said the service was delayed by more than six hours but would travel on to Warsaw after border checks were completed.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Poland’s interior minister Marcin Kierwinski said one drone struck near the Dorohusk-Yagodyn border crossing, while the other hit the passenger train.

“We are treating these events with the utmost seriousness. The situation is being monitored on an ongoing basis,” Kierwinski said.

News.title: I was nine-months-pregnant when my husband’s heart stopped – on a frantic 999 call I battled to save his life
News.content:
ON DEATH’S DOOR I was nine-months-pregnant when my husband’s heart stopped – on a frantic 999 call I battled to save his life

A HEAVILY pregnant mum-to-be gave her husband lifesaving CPR after he went into cardiac arrest in the middle of the night.

Emma King had by chance got up to go to the toilet in the early hours when she noticed partner Sam was barely conscious and making “weird noises” as he gasped for breath, with his eyes rolling back.



She dialled 999 and the call handler instructed her to begin doing chest compressions – which continued once paramedics arrived for an unheard of two hours, with little chance given of survival.

Emma, 27, who had previously been first-aid trained, was talked through the process over the phone, having clambered over Sam, also 27, on the bed, despite her large baby bump.



She told The Sun: “Ideally, if you’re giving CPR, they’re meant to be on a hard floor, but Sam was on our memory foam bed.

“So I had to keep adjusting my knees… I was physically bouncing the bed pretty much.”



Emma continued: “The call handler never told me to give breath, she just said to perform chest compressions.

“I knew where to put my hands and that you can give as much force as you can – the harder you do it, the better.

“It was a case of the timing, she made me repeat the timing out loud.

“Every time I’d do a compression, I’d go ‘push, push, push, push’ so she knew whether I was doing it at the right time.”



The emergency unfolded at around 4am on April 3 this year at the couple’s townhouse in Hedge End, Hampshire – days before they were due to welcome first child Sophie.

Emma added: “I had no idea he was in cardiac arrest at first.

“It was waking up to go to the toilet in the middle of the night, and then Sam gasping for breath and me thinking ‘what the hell?’



“I’ve turned my phone to look at him and his eyes have gone back in his head.”

Emma said the call handler “saved his life by telling me to do CPR”.

Ambulance and fire teams arrived within minutes and, struggling to restart his heart, medics worked on Sam for two hours, including giving him 11 zaps with a defibrillator, and using a hands-free mechanical chest compression called LUCAS.

His heart was showing little signs of life and the couple later learned continuing CPR for so long is rare.

The paramedics would’ve stopped but having intubated Sam, they detected he was still producing CO2, meaning his body was taking in oxygen.



What is CPR and how to learn it CPR stands for cardiopulmonary resuscitation, an emergency life-saving procedure performed when someone’s breathing or heartbeat has stopped. It keeps blood moving, provides oxygen and buys time. Learning CPR is one of the most impactful skills you can acquire, and you can start learning right now for free or choose an in-person certified course depending on your goals. Here are the primary ways to learn CPR, ranging from quick online tutorials to official certifications: Free Online Training (Quick & Convenient) If you want to learn the basics immediately without a formal certification, excellent digital tools are available: British Heart Foundation (BHF): You can use their free, interactive RevivR Online CPR Training Tool. It takes just 15 minutes using your smartphone or tablet and a cushion to practice on. It teaches you how to recognise cardiac arrest, make an emergency call, perfect your compression technique, and use a defibrillator.

You can use their free, interactive RevivR Online CPR Training Tool. It takes just 15 minutes using your smartphone or tablet and a cushion to practice on. It teaches you how to recognise cardiac arrest, make an emergency call, perfect your compression technique, and use a defibrillator. Video Guides: For a quick visual overview of the technique, you can watch step-by-step demonstrations via the St John Ambulance CPR Guide or standard medical walkthroughs like this First Aid Tips CPR Video In-Person Courses (For Certification & Workplace Needs) If you need an official certificate for work, or if you prefer hands-on practice with a medical mannequin, you should book an in-person class: St John Ambulance: They are the UK’s leading first aid training provider and offer everything from basic community sessions to formal workplace certifications (such as Emergency First Aid at Work).

They are the UK’s leading first aid training provider and offer everything from basic community sessions to formal workplace certifications (such as Emergency First Aid at Work). The British Red Cross: They provide robust, locally available first aid courses covering adult, child, and infant CPR.

They provide robust, locally available first aid courses covering adult, child, and infant CPR. Community Groups: Organisations like the East Anglian Air Ambulance and local rescue services frequently run free or low-cost 1-hour community workshops.

An ultrasound later showed it was “fluttering”, meaning, despite no pulse or blood pressure “there was still some electrical activity”, explained Sam.

“If they could restart it, then I had a chance, although a bloody small one, of surviving,” he said. “So they did CPR for two hours, which is just crazy.”

On realising there was little more they could do outside of hospital, the paramedics had to manoeuvre the 6 ‘2 patient down multiple flights of stairs, with the bedroom in a loft conversion, and navigate tight corners, while still doing CPR in a relay-style routine.

During the journey to hospital, the LUCAS device even ran out of battery, meaning medics had to return to manual compressions in the back of the ambulance.

They arrived at Southampton General Hospital around 6am – but Sam said his understanding is there was still little hope of survival.



He said: “They were basically like, ‘we’ll give it a go, but he’s just going to die’. There’s no way that people survive that.”

Sam’s heart did finally restart once he was in hospital but there was a high likelihood of brain damage, and he was put on dialysis with his heart, lungs, liver, kidneys and gut all failing.

“It was a roll of the dice even on the ambulance ride,” he said.



Luckily, on-duty doctor Edward Langford, part of South Central Ambulance Charity, who was among the medics who scrambled to the scene, thought ahead, getting an extracorporeal membrane oxygenation device (ECMO) – shipped to Southampton from St Thomas Hospital in London.

There are very few of the mechanical heart and lungs, but it arrived as Sam was in surgery that afternoon.

He said: “I’ve got these big scars on my thighs because they go into your main arteries and plug in this big lung to replace your heart and lungs.”

That evening, Sam was blue-lighted to London where he remained in a coma until May 12.

Four days after his cardiac arrest, Emma – who had her care transferred to London – gave birth to daughter Sophie on April 6, after a 36-hour labour.



Four hours after Sam woke up, she was brought down with the little tot to see him, and he burst into tears.

Laughing, he said: “There’s this video of me, I’m being unventilated, I’m all yellow because my liver doesn’t work, I’ve got this stuff in my thighs, it’s not pretty – and Sophie was held up to me.

“They placed Sophie on me and apparently I cried. Emma said ‘Sam, Sophie’s here.’”



Emma said: “It was one of the most overwhelming experiences that any person could ever go through.”

At that point, the doctors were unsure of Sam’s brain capacity, and whether he would recover.

Emma admitted she had been worried as time went on, and was even thinking about having family move in to help look after Sam long-term.

“To begin with, you think so far into the future and you’re like, oh God, how are you going to cope?” she said.

“But because he was so unwell, I kind of forgot or I ignored any thoughts about his brain activity. There were so many other things wrong with him and it was about would he survive?”



But, miraculously, Sam appears to have made a full recovery, with tests still ongoing as to the cause of the sudden cardiac arrest.

Sam left hospital on May 6 after 33 days and has had a cardioverter-defibrillator fitted similar to footballer Christian Eriksen who suffered a cardiac arrest on the pitch during Euro 2020, and the device can restart his heart if it ever stops again.

He remained on dialysis while his kidney function recovered and is now even back to work and playing sports – as well as helping with baby Sophie.

“I’m not allowed to hold her stood up,” he said. “Because if I have another cardiac arrest, my fibrillation will kick in and I’ll collapse.

“So I can just have her in my arms while I’m sitting down.”



The couple – both software developers who met on Tinder in 2018 before marrying last year – are taking things slowly, with Sam admitting “we’re incredibly lucky”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sam has since met with the 11-strong team of members of the South Central Ambulance Service, as well as the Hampshire and Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service and an emergency doctor who saved his life.

He said: “I’ll never forget the second chance they’ve given me.”

News.title: Brit ‘killed by Afghan & hid in suitcase could have been forced to take anti-depressant to calm down on day of murder’
News.content:
A BRIT aid worker found dead and stuffed in a suitcase may have been forced to take anti-depressants on the day of her alleged murder.

Elisabeth Ross’ body was found dumped in a derelict building in Athens on July 18, with Afghan national Sharif Ahmadzai accused of her killing.



The former boxer, 26, is now languishing in a notorious hellhole prison – where The Sun revealed that inmates have pummelled the “lady killer”.

Traces of the anti-depressant Fluoxetine were found in Elisabeth’s system during toxicological tests as forensic teams probe her cause of death.



An insider told The Sun: “It was only a small amount, nothing to suggest long-term usage.

“Police believe she could have taken it, or been forced to take it, on the day [she died] to calm down.”

Loved ones now face an agonising wait to determine how Elisabeth, 38, died after more forensic tests have been ordered.

“It was always thought toxicological tests would shed light on how she died but they have proved to be inconclusive,” said sources with knowledge of the forensic investigation.



“More lab analysis has been requested after traces of Fluoxetine were found.”

Fluoxetine is frequently used to treat depression and obsessive-compulsive disorder.

Ahmadzai has been held pending trial on charges of intentional homicide, but robustly denied killing Elisabeth.



The refugee, who had lived and worked in Greece for years helping refugees, confessed to transferring the Scot to the derelict site.

He claimed to have found Elisabeth’s lifeless body at a flat used by him and his American wife, Alaina Hall, to hold meetings for their NGO, Love Only Nation, set up to help refugees.

Hopes of pinpointing the cause of death were dashed when pathologists called to examine the Brit’s body said it was impossible due to advanced decomposition.

Without any outward signs of injury, experts said Ross had probably died as a result of suffocation.

In the three days after her death and before she was found, Ahmadzai admitted using her credit cards to steal more than £8,500.



He also used her phone to send misleading messages to family and friends, believed to be a ploy to stop them reporting her missing.

But police say they are still flummoxed by the lack of motive for the crime.

“We believe he did it but the question is why?” one said.



“His wife assisted us in our inquiry but she is non-plussed too.”

The mystery deepened as it emerged that Ahmadzai was “badly beaten up” in Korydallos prison where he has been detained pending trial.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Ahmadzai’s lawyers had previously demanded the Scottish-born charity worker’s health records be released as part of the investigation.

A cop said: “The latest findings have not changed our view that he is the culprit who cut this young woman’s life short.”

News.title: Restaurant owners team up to get revenge on the 'Bonnie and Clyde of dine and dash'
News.content:
Restaurant owners team up to get revenge on the 'Bonnie and Clyde of dine and dash'

One half of a pair, who left six restaurants without paying in one month, has now been caught after business owners worked together to try and bring the duo to justice

View 3 Images A couple who dined and dashed at six venues have been caugth in Spain (stock) (Image: Getty)

One half of a couple dubbed the ‘Bonnie and Clyde’ of dine and dash was caught after the duo fled six venues in one part of Spain without paying their bill.

‌



The man, 40, who was arrested on September 4, was one half of a duo who skipped out on bills at restaurants and cafes in the Alt Emporda region of the European country, near the country’s border with France.

‌



The string of dine and dash incidents reportedly happened over a month and the affected parties were reportedly in contact with each other during this time, before it all ended at Pizzeria Il Nonno.

‌



It was at this venue that the man was confronted, then chased, by the manager before being arrested by the Castello d’Empuries Local police.

L'independant reports that the couple had also attempted to pull the same stunt at places along the Costa Brava in Catalonia, five of which were in the coastal town of Empuriabrava.

View 3 Images Most of the incidents happened around Empuriabrava (stock) (Image: Getty)

‌



The first of these alleged incidents was reported on August 17 where, having requested to have their coffee outside, the couple exited leaving the Vilabertran venue €95.40 (£81.89) out of pocket.

Later, they would visit the L’Empuria Beach café where the woman left, followed by the man, who claimed to a waitress that he was leaving for cigarettes. They venue was left with a €75 (£64.38) unpaid bill.

Other venues affected, reports El Gerio Digital, were The Loft, Internet Café, and Restaurant Dlux alongside the restaurant in Vilabertran.

‌



However, it all came to a head at the aforementioned Pizzeria Il Nonno over a bill of €55.10 (£47.30).

View 3 Images The man was later caught by local police (stock) (Image: Getty)

Following the events of the couple’s near month-long spree of fleeing, the six restaurants are now working together to assemble a detailed picture of what happened and how much money was lost, along with evidence from security footage.

‌



It is not yet known what has happened to the arrested individual’s alleged accomplice and whether or not she, in turn, has been caught.

As well as being held by the authorities over the dine and dash incidents, the man was also arrested on a separate offence.

The man, who has not been named, was arrested over allegedly breaching an active restraining order in relation to his former partner and currently has a police record. The precise details of this alleged offence are not known.
