Labour have said that the “questions keep piling up” for Nigel Farage after footage emerged of him admitting he knew Russians used cryptocurrency to cheat Ukraine war sanctions, but invested in the sector anyway.

In an unearthed 2022 interview given just days after Vladimir Putin declared war on Kyiv, Mr Farage credited Russian sanction busting investment for a 15 per cent spike in crypto values.

Despite knowing crypto was aiding the Russian war effort, Mr Farage went on to invest hundreds of thousands of pounds in the sector.

A Labour Party spokesperson said “Pandora’s box has been opened when it comes to Farage’s relationship with crypto”, adding that his investment in the sector after he knew Russia was using it to break sanctions “raises serious questions about his moral judgement”.

The row comes as Reform UK have taken two separate donations of £36m from crypto billionaires Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo with housing secretary Angela Rayner suggesting a new law could “retrospectively” block Reform accepting the money.

open image in gallery Farage is facing questions about his judgement ( Reuters )

Speaking to financial firm Southbank Investment Research in 2022, Mr Farage explained how crypto exchanges were not banning Russian assets, and that Russians transferring cash into crypto were behind a rally in that market.

The Reform UK leader said: “The crypto markets are not going along with this complete ban on Russian assets. And maybe one of the reasons why crypto, after a big fall, has rallied, I don't know, about 15 per cent this week, something like that, is we're beginning to see Russians transfer assets into crypto wallets, into crypto assets.”

Mr Farage appeared at the Southbank Investment Research event on 4 March 2022 after the firm paid him to publish the “Fortune and Freedom” investment newsletter, which saw him offer market tips to subscribers paying a £199 annual fee.

The issue of Russia using crypto was today raised by Tory shadow foreign secretary Tom Tugendhat on the BBC’s Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg show.

He said: “The idea that we should have loose regulations on crypto is a strange one, given that when I set up the Defending Democracy Task Force as security minister, we followed Russian mafia money going through crypto, going through various European countries to pay for assassinations in the UK or sabotaging Europe.”

Despite acknowledging that Russians was using crypto to get around sanctions, Mr Farage has invested heavily in the crypto market. The Reform UK leader has invested £265,000 in bitcoin treasury firm Stack BTC, run by former Tory chancellor Kwasi Kwarteng. Mr Farage was also the public face of Stack’s £2m bitcoin purchase in April 2026, though this did not use his personal funds.

He has also announced that he would liberalise the crypto market if Reform wins power, with the party having already accepted vast sums in donations from those in the sector.

Late last year Mr Farage told a crypto conference “I am your champion”. In October he told a blockchain conference that “people should hold crypto as part of their portfolio”. At another event a month later he admitted “I have got some crypto investments that are long-term".

open image in gallery Putin used crypto to evade sanctions ( Reuters )

Mr Farage is under investigation for an undeclared £5m donation from Reform’s biggest donor, Christopher Harborne, who is a cryptocurrency billionaire.

A November 2025 National Crime Agency report found that Tether – the stablecoin Mr Harborne holds a reported 12 per cent stake in – had been used to help the Russian war effort against Ukraine.

Concerns about Mr Farage’s attitude to Russia come after the former leader of Reform in Wales, Nathan Gill, was imprisoned for taking a Russian bribe. In the past, Mr Farage has said that he “admires” President Vladimir Putin.

A Labour Party spokesperson said: “Pandora’s box has been opened when it comes to Farage’s relationship with crypto. The fact that he welcomed Russians using crypto to break sanctions in the immediate aftermath of Putin's invasion of Ukraine, simply because it boosted the value of crypto investments, raises serious questions about his moral judgement.

“Yet again it looks like he’s backing up his billionaire crypto mates, while potentially undermining Britain’s support for Ukraine. This is just another example of why he’s completely unfit to be prime minister.”

They added: "The questions keep piling up about Farage's finances, but he still can’t answer them.”

The Independent has approached Reform UK for comment.

Marking the 25th anniversary of the 11 September terrorist attacks in his native country, Pope Leo XIV, history's first American pope, called for a renewed commitment to peace on Sunday.

Addressing gathered crowds in English from his studio window overlooking St. Peter’s Square, the Chicago-born pope made his first public comments commemorating the occasion following his traditional Sunday noon blessing.

"Two days ago marked the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks in the United States of America," Leo said. "I renew my prayers for those who lost their lives and for those who continue to bear the wounds of that tragic day."

He went on to state that "at a time when conflict and violence afflict so many of our brothers and sisters, I invite everyone to pray that the Lord will bestow his gift of peace upon the world."

Switching to Italian, he added: "The memory of the tragic events of 25 years ago pushes us to renew our commitment to peace, above all with prayer."

Pope Leo XIV addresses the crowd from the window of the apostolic palace overlooking St Peter's Square during his Sunday Angelus prayer at the Vatican on September 13 ( AFP/Getty )

When the attacks occurred on 11 September 2001, the former Robert Prevost was in Rome for a major assembly of his Augustinian religious order, where he was serving as the Chicago provincial leader. On 14 September, his birthday, Prevost was elected superior of the entire order, holding the role across two consecutive terms until 2012.

On Sunday, Vatican News republished extracts of his initial homily as superior, preached on 21 September 2001, in which the future American pope considered the impact of the attacks.

"We cannot fail to remember the tragic events that shook the United States on Sept. 11," he said in his homily. "The violence that the world witnessed last week in the United States is a tragic expression of a series of problems that are becoming increasingly acute everywhere.

"Hatred and violence will continue to grow as long as so many people are forced to live in extreme poverty and are oppressed by so many forms of injustice."

News.title: Tora Bora’s last midwife struggles under Taliban rule as aid runs dry
News.content:
The small clinic, crowded with pregnant women, sits in the shadow of Tora Bora in eastern Afghanistan. Twenty-five years ago, those mountains commanded the attention of the world’s most powerful military. Roughly 15 miles from the clinic, in the Tora Bora cave complex, Osama bin Laden was believed to be hiding as American bombs rained down in the hunt for the architect of 9/11.

Today, another consequence of the West’s long entanglement with Afghanistan is playing out beneath those same mountains – in the struggle to keep mothers and babies alive.

In the baking courtyard of Gandab Kharoti health centre, dozens of women enveloped in sapphire blue burqas sit shoulder to shoulder beneath trees waiting to see Shila Ibrahimi, a 27-year-old midwife.

The women rest against walls, dusty, barefoot children play, and mothers cradle sick babies beneath folds of cloth. Some have walked for hours through the mountains to reach her.

Among them is Fawzia, 30, seven-and-a-half months pregnant with her seventh child. Suffering from headaches, she has walked for miles through the heat.

Her husband works far from the village, so she makes the journey with her children and mother-in-law, hoping the Taliban do not stop her for the “crime” of travelling without a male escort.

Under the Taliban’s morality rules, women face restrictions on travelling alone, while UN monitors have documented the regime’s morality inspectors ordering some health facilities not to treat unaccompanied women.

But enforcement varies and Fawzia says nobody challenged her on her journey here. Asked where she would give birth if the clinic closed she says: “We have nowhere else to go. We cannot afford that. We are poor.”

News.title: Springboks look like World Cup champions elect… again
News.content:
“South Africa are very good at creating opportunities and taking their chances, and so they scored it under the posts. That was a big moment in the game, and so we know if we can do a couple of things a bit better, limit their opportunities, and be a little bit more clinical, the result could go another way. But they are a very good side, and they scramble really well, and yeah I think the better side probably won in the end.

“We could talk about scrums, but we will have to be better. They have got a great scrum, they have got a great maul, so our ability to stay in front of that maul is important. And when we did that, we limited their ability to hurt us, and likewise at scrum time. The easiest way is to limit those occurrences. So, if we are more accurate, there are fewer scrums and greater continuity for us, and we do not kick the ball out.

“There are fewer lineouts for them, and discipline comes into it. You cannot just make their strengths disappear. But our job is to limit the amount of opportunities they get. I think on our ball, the scrum was reasonably solid. We got it badly wrong on one, then got punished with one of their feeds, and so look, it is a weapon for them, and that is the challenge. We want high continuity. If you make an error, they get to go to a set-piece. They get a penalty off that. They march up the field, and so it is still an area we are going to have to be better at.”

News.title: Sabalenka smashes racket and swears at cameraman after Rybakina clinches US Open
News.content:
Sabalenka and Rybankina have now played four slam finals, with the spoils evenly shared after this 6-4, 5-7, 6-2 grapple in the Apple – as a boxing promoter might have referred to it.

There is certainly something pugilistic about the way these two go toe-to-toe. The emphasis is on landing the first blow, so the rallies tend not to be particularly long: only four points out of 193 went beyond nine shots. But the precision of the ball-striking was breathtaking. At one point in the first set, Rybakina had hit eight winners to just a single unforced error – the sort of ratio to send coaches starry-eyed.

Sabalanka arrived on court in her showy jewellery – which is worth more than £300,000 for the full set, according to the manufacturers – and an orange Nike dress that put one in mind of the Dutch national football team. “Total tennis” may have been the goal, but sometimes your opponent doesn’t allow you to play. This was the case in the early stages as Rybakina – whose own yellow-and-black outfit evoked the natural warning signs of a wasp or hornet – seemed to flush every ball right out of the centre of her racket.

Sabalenka actually did a sterling job of digging herself out of trouble in her service games, saving four of five break points in the first set. But this still wasn’t enough, given that Rybakina was defending her own serve with the same serenity that characterises everything she does.

News.title: Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions
News.content:
Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

“I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

Kick off 8pm.

News.title: £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham
News.content:
Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

“Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

For Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he said. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”

News.title: Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players
News.content:
Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

News.title: Lando Norris on pole for Spanish GP but adds voice to critics of ‘Madring’
News.content:
Red Bull’s Max Verstappen predicted that overtaking would be “practically impossible” in the race. “[The Madring] has a tendency of maybe creating some big shunts in some places,” the Dutchman said. “It reminds me a little bit of Jeddah in a way – fast corners and the walls being very close.

“The only thing that’s already a bit disappointing is that many of the braking zones are angled. This means it’s practically impossible to attack a competitor because you’re braking and simultaneously turning right or left. And that’s the worst thing you can do if you want to create an overtaking opportunity.”

Norris agreed with Verstappen that it would be very difficult to overtake, although that is no bad thing for him provided he can hang on to the lead at the start.

The Briton, though, described the decision to build what is now the longest pit lane on the F1 calendar as a big disappointment.

“I think it has a lot of potential,” Norris said of the Madring. “Just certain things need to be improved. Like the pit lane, which is like six kilometres long. It’s the longest pit lane of the year and the biggest pit loss of the year [in terms of the time it will take to pit – an estimated 25 seconds]. So that just makes overtaking worse. Not overtaking, but it makes the desire to box and do different strategies worse.

“You know, if we’re going to build a new track and spend so much money in building a new track, this is probably one of the main factors, I would say, is you have a short pit lane so people can pit and you then create overtaking.”

Norris described his pole lap as “one of the best laps of his career” and his team principal Andrea Stella fully agreed, describing it as “a masterpiece”.

News.title: Bomb squad rescues rusty Red Roses
News.content:
Mia Venner, Sadia Kabeya, Lucy Packer and Claudia Moloney-MacDonald went over for further tries to add to player-of-the-match Abi Burton’s first-half score.

Moloney-MacDonald’s try wide out on the left was a show-stopper for the crowd of 9,251 in the North West and demonstrated that England have style to go with solidity. But it was the power game that did for Australia.

The Wallaroos scored tries of their own through Faliki Pohiva and Eva Karpani but spent the vast majority of the game manning the defensive barricades. They did so admirably for 40 minutes but when the dam wall blew it blew spectacularly.

They did not help themselves with sin-binnings in either half for Samantha Wood and Karpani, but over 80 minutes the odds will always be stacked in favour of the full-time side against the part-timers.

“The reality is that even at our best we’re probably not good enough. We will be,” said Tim Walsh, Rugby Australia’s director of women’s high performance. “We need an environment where they can concentrate on being full-time athletes. That’s the vision Rugby Australia have and that’s where we’re headed.”

The game was England’s first with the smaller ball being trialled in the women’s game by World Rugby and they only converted four of their eight tries, a statistic which may be seized upon by those who do not care for it. A rugby pitch is not a sterile laboratory though and the swirling, blustery conditions should be taken into account in any dissection of its value.

Sports.title: ‘What are they thinking’ – Horror Coventry vs Brighton kit clash making fans ‘want to turn it off’
Sports.content:
SKY SPORTS’ Super Sunday coverage has not started as they might have expected, as fans have slated a kit clash in the early kick-off.

Coventry host Brighton, but a lot of fans can’t tell who’s who, with questions being asked of Premier League organisers.



Brighton’s new third kit, featuring a solid turquoise colour throughout is confusingly similar to Coventry’s navy shorts and dark blue socks.

And despite organisers clearly not clocking it beforehand, you bet the fans have.



Viewers took to X to vent their frustrations at the kit clash.

One wrote: “Kit clash in Coventry/Brighton is awful what are they thinking.”



A second said: “Jesus thats a shocking kit clash for Coventry Brighton. Who approved that?”

A third posted: “What in the kit clash is going on with Coventry vs Brighton?”

A fourth added: “Stupid kit clash in Coventry v Brighton game.”

And a fifth even said: “This kit clash is making me want to turn it off.”



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Fans aren’t impressed with the kits, but Coventry boss Frank Lampard also won’t be impressed with his team as they trail 2-0.

Charalampos Kostoulas and Malick Yalcouye bagged the goals for Brighton, who look to be taking all three points back to the South coast.

A victory puts Fabian Hurzeler‘s team in an impressive 4th place.

Meanwhile Coventry are yet to score a Premier League goal this campaign, following a tough opening set of fixtures and sit rock bottom.

Sports.title: Arsenal ‘monitoring’ Como star Nico Paz but Real Madrid hold first refusal on £68.7million January transfer
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are reportedly monitoring Como star Nico Paz ahead of a potential January swoop.

But the Gunners could face a major obstacle in their pursuit of the highly-rated Argentina international, with Real Madrid retaining significant control over his future.



Paz, 22, has established himself as one of Serie A’s brightest young talents since leaving the Bernabeu for Como in 2024.

And according to reports in Spain, Arsenal are keeping a close eye on the attacking midfielder and could make their move in January.



However, Real Madrid have an £68.7million buy-back option which becomes active in the summer of 2027.

That means the Spanish giants could potentially bring their former academy star back to Madrid rather than allow him to move elsewhere.



Paz opted to remain with Como this summer despite speculation surrounding his future following another impressive campaign in Italy.

Real Madrid initially had the option to bring him back for around £9m but decided against triggering it.

Instead, Como reportedly paid £51.5m to take full control of the player, with Real securing their new £70m buy-back option for next summer.

The arrangement means Arsenal’s pursuit could ultimately depend on whether Real decide they want Paz back at the Bernabeu.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Madrid could also potentially activate their option before deciding whether to keep Paz or listen to offers from other clubs interested in the midfielder.

Paz himself was keen to remain in Italy, where he has flourished under former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas.

Real confirmed the decision for him to stay at Como was made “at the player’s own request”.

The Argentina star has become a central figure in Fabregas’ side and helped fire Como into the Champions League.



Paz scored six goals and provided eight assists across 35 Serie A appearances during the 2024-25 campaign.

He then took another huge step forward last season, registering 12 goals and six assists from another 35 league appearances.

And the former Real Madrid youngster has already opened his account this term, scoring a stunning goal in Como’s 4-1 victory over Genoa.

Paz also wears the No10 shirt at Como and has a contract with the Italian club running until June 2028.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace must sort out their leaky defence or face relegation as Pierre Sage issues rallying cry to his players
Sports.content:
AFTER just four Premeir League games it is Crystal clear that Palace must sort out their leaky defence – or face relegation.

The Eagles have been flying high over the last two seasons with historic FA Cup and Conference League victories.



Those title-winning cup runs were built on a solid foundation with the likes of Marc Guehi and Maxence Lacroix.

But seeing the best assets stripped away without adequate replacements could see them come back down to earth with a bang… in the Championship.



Under new manager Pierre Sage, Palace have the worst defensive record in the top flight after the 3-2 defeat to Ipswich, conceding no fewer than two in every game so far and 11 in total.

The Frenchman arrived at Selhurst Park with a stellar reputation after guiding Lens to second in Ligue 1 and their first-ever Coupe de France title last season.

In his pre-match notes, Sage explained the need for his players to form connections.

But the 47-year-old has contradicted that as he is yet to name the same three centre-backs for his 3-4-2-1 formation in any of his five games in charge.

That trend will continue after Axel Disasi’s sending off against Ipswich, while Palace also have a Europa League campaign to contend with, starting with a clash against Lech Poznan on Thursday.

Sage admitted he would need to rotate the team for freshness but also emphasised the need for stability, saying: “Yeah, we have to continue (changing) because of the red card. But we need stability with a lot of games.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“We need rotation for freshness, but I have to find the best back three of the moment and have some little rotations to be more balanced.

“Today (against Ipswich), I think we were more balanced than every other game. We concede the goals, but we don’t concede too many chances, or less than the other games.

“It’s a defensive unit, yes, but now the problem is in another part of the play. We concede too many crosses and we don’t win the ball in the box.

“There’s two new problems. The consequence of what we did well, because we closed the play inside, now it’s clear we have to be more efficient in the consequence of that.”



Sage hasn’t been helped by the loss of England goalkeeper and captain Dean Henderson through an ankle injury.

There is seemingly an issue of commitment with some stars too, with Sage revealing he dropped Jaydee Canvot because he “needs more from him”.

On the decision to drop the 20-year-old, who had previously started all three league games, he explained: “It was a sporting decision.

“I didn’t take him in the team because of his game against Fulham and what he did during the week.



“I spoke with him, I want more, I need more from him. I’m sure he’s able to, and I wait for his good reaction from Monday.”

Sports.title: Preston sack manager Paul Heckingbottom after woeful start to Championship season sees them in relegation zone
Sports.content:
PRESTON North End have parted ways with boss Paul Heckingbottom.

The Championship side lost 1-0 to Lincoln City on Saturday, making it six defeats in seven games.

Heckingbottom will abandon Deepdale after their woeful start left them second-botttom in the table.



The club statement read: “Preston North End Football Club have today taken the decision to part company with Paul Heckingbottom as First Team Football Manager.



“Football is a results business and despite significant investment in the playing squad since Paul joined, the results during 2026 and the start of this current campaign have not been acceptable.”

The statement continued: “Paul leaves us with our thanks and best wishes. His professionalism and work ethic during his time with us have been second to none.

“As a result of this decision Stuart McCall has also left the Club today.



“We similarly thank Stuart for his contribution over the last two years and wish him all the best for the future.

“We will now look to appoint a new manager as soon as possible but until such time as we do Jason Euell will take charge of first team matters on an interim basis.”

It was Lincoln’s victory that rubberstamped Heckingbottom’s P45.

Speaking the BBC after the 1-0 defeat on Saturday, the sacked head coach said: “It was no surprise in terms of how difficult that game was and the pattern of the game.



“We are really frustrated that 90 per cent of the time their threats, because we limited the number of corners and set-plays, we did deal with them.”

The 49-year-old was handed the reins of the Lancashire outfit in August 2024.

North End got off to a decent start but it dwindled as they were dragged into a relegation battle.

It was not until the final day, that the Lilywhites secured safety.

Heckingbottom’s predecessor, Ryan Lowe, was asked to leave after just one game of the Championship season.



More to follow.

Sports.title: Arsenal wonderkid Marli Salmon, 17, braced for Carabao Cup bow after Ben White injury as Arteta faces selection dilemma
Sports.content:
ARSENAL wonderkid Marli Salmon could be handed a surprise Carabao Cup start after Ben White picked up a groin problem.

SunSport understands White will be assessed ahead of Tuesday night’s trip to Ipswich after being forced off at half-time during yesterday’s 2-0 win over Sunderland.



Jurrien Timber replaced him at half-time in the 2-0 win against Sunderland yesterday, but the Dutchman is unlikely to be risked from the start after only recently returning from injury.

That could leave Mikel Arteta with a major selection headache at right-back and force the Arsenal boss to turn to highly-rated academy star Salmon.



The 17-year-old was in action for the Under-21s against Chelsea yesterday as he continues to impress after making his senior breakthrough last season.

Salmon has trained regularly with Arteta’s first team for months and could now be in line for his first competitive appearance of the campaign.



Timber would normally be Arsenal’s first-choice right-back, but his own injury problems have restricted him to just three appearances in the last six months.

One of those came as a late substitute in the Champions League final defeat on penalties against Paris Saint-Germain in May.

The 25-year-old was rushed back from injury and subsequently missed the Netherlands’ World Cup campaign as a result.

White, meanwhile, had started the season strongly before the groin issue forced him out at the interval against Sunderland.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And with Cristhian Mosquera also sidelined while recovering from a hamstring strain suffered against Aston Villa at the end of last month, Arteta’s right-back options are suddenly looking thin.

Salmon could therefore get another taste of senior football barely two weeks after celebrating his 17th birthday by signing his first professional contract with the club.

The Hale End academy graduate made his first-team debut against Club Brugge in the Champions League last season.



He went on to make four senior appearances in total, also featuring in FA Cup wins over Portsmouth, Wigan and Mansfield.

Salmon came through the same Arsenal age group as fellow wonderkid Max Dowman and has spent much of the past few months around Arteta’s senior squad.

Now, with White facing a fitness check, Timber unlikely to be pushed, and Mosquera still recovering, Salmon is suddenly much closer to a first-team call-up than he might have expected.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo demands lifetime bans for Saudi fans behind sick Diogo Jota chants directed towards Ruben Neves
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO has demanded lifetime bans for fans who targeted Ruben Neves with sick Diogo Jota chants during Al-Hilal’s Saudi Pro League clash.

Al-Taawoun supporters could be heard shouting “Jota! Jota! Jota!” towards the former Wolves midfielder during Saturday’s match.



An angry Neves, who carried close pal Jota’s coffin at his funeral, responded by making a “God is watching you” gesture before sarcastically applauding the supporters.

And the 29-year-old later said as he made his way through the mixed zone: “I just hope they don’t go to pray later.”



The incident sparked fury online – and Al-Nassr superstar Ronaldo has now joined those demanding punishment.

Commenting on an Instagram post calling for action, the 233-cap Portugal legend wrote: “The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour.



“This is no longer football and there have to be limits.

“People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again.”

Some have claimed the chants were intended as a tribute to Liverpool hero Jota, who tragically died aged 28 alongside his brother Andre Silva in a car crash in Spain in July 2025.

But they were widely condemned given Neves’ close relationship with his late team-mate.



Neves and Jota spent three seasons together at Wolves and also shared a dressing room with Portugal.



Following Jota’s death, an emotional Neves vowed to remain close to his friend’s family.

He wrote: “More than a friendship, we’re family, and we won’t stop it just because now you decided to sign a contract a little further away from us.

“I’m going to make sure you’re always present and I’ll make sure that your loved ones never lack anything while you’re there, far away but thinking of us, waiting for us.

“Life has brought us together and now it can’t tear us apart.”

Liverpool later retired Jota’s No20 shirt across all levels of the club, the first time in the Reds’ history that a squad number had been permanently withdrawn.



Saturday’s ugly scenes overshadowed an emphatic 6-0 victory for Al-Hilal, with Neves setting up Ollie Watkins for the opener before Gabriel Martinelli bagged a hat-trick.

The victory sent Al-Hilal top of the Saudi Pro League after winning six of their opening seven matches.

Sports.title: Sunderland should never have had a penalty against Arsenal – Ballard fouled Konsa first, admits ex-Prem referee Halsey
Sports.content:
FORMER Premier League referee Mark Halsey believes the officials made an error yesterday when they awarded Sunderland a penalty against Arsenal.

The reigning champions won the game 2-0 at the Stadium of Light, but were pushed all the way by the Black Cats.



Former Newcastle midfielder Bruno Guimaraes opened the scoring in the 58th minute – just two minutes before the game’s most controversial moment when Sunderland were awarded a penalty.

The players in question were Ezri Konsa and Dan Ballard, with the former adjudged to have pulled the latter to the ground after Kevin Danso launched a long throw towards the near post – where the tugging took place.



But it appeared to be six of one half a dozen of the other, and former Prem ref Halsey weighed in on the incident.

Halsey exclusively told SunSport: “There was a controversial incident in the Sunderland vs Arsenal at the Stadium of Light… second half, 56th minute, Sunderland were awarded a penalty for a foul on Sunderland’s Ballard by Konsa.

“Now, when you look at an incident, you can clearly see in my opinion, that Ballard committed the first offence.

“He’s got hold of Konsa’s arm, so he’s pulled him around and they’ve both ended up on the floor. Then it looks like Konsa has tumbled into Ballard.

“For me, I think that Ballard has committed the first offence and it’s not a penalty. Should VAR have got involved? Was it a clear and obvious error by the match referee?

“Now, I know that they’ve set a high bar now in VAR getting involved but I think that was one where they should have got involved because Ballard committed the first offence. So for me, it wasn’t a penalty and VAR should have got involved.”



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

In the end, the penalty had no imapct on the result.

David Raya made a sensational diving save to tip Enzo Le Fee’s penalty on to the post before Arsenal immediately went up the other end and scored thanks to Guimaraes’ piledriver from 25 yards out.

Sunderland huffed and puffed chasing an equaliser, but Arsenal’s defence was resolute.



Then in the final minute of stoppage time, the Gunners were awarded a spot kick when Reinildo Mandava brought down Bukayo Saka in the box.

Referee Craig Pawson followed it up by sending off the Mozambican left-back – a decision Halsey again didn’t agree with.

He added: “Arsenal were awarded a penalty later on in the game, which was a clear penalty. But I felt that the second yellow card for Reinildo Mandava was not a second yellow card, it was a careless challenge and a penalty was a sufficient punishment.”

Sports.title: Jimenez hits 90th-minute winner for Wolves at Sheff Utd
Sports.content:
Raul Jimenez came off the bench to score a 90th-minute winner and earn Wolves a 1-0 win over Sheffield United.

Cesar Peixoto's side had controversially been denied a penalty shortly after the restart, when Mark McGuinness handled in the box.

But a game of few clear-cut chances was settled when Jimenez swept in his third goal of the season from close range.

Image: Raul Jimenez celebrates his late match-winner for Wolves

The Blades had both scored and conceded in 14 of their last 15 Championship games at Bramall Lane - so perhaps there was always an inevitability that pattern would not continue.

Chris Wilder's side had just two touches in the opposition box in the first half and generated just 0.06 xG, while at the other end, Marshall Munetsi was Wolves' biggest threat, though Michael Cooper was rarely tested.

With 50 minutes on the clock, Mateus Mane flicked the ball towards goal, with McGuinness' outstretched hand diverting it behind. Referee Rob Jones awarded a corner, nothing more.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wolves were denied a penalty after this incident during their Sky Bet Championship game against Sheffield United.

Speaking on Sky Sports Football, co-commentator Gary Rowett said: "His arm comes out, it hits him on the end of the arm. I think Sheffield United have probably got away with one there."

Sheffield United debutant Jordan Ayew almost had the perfect introduction when he drove in from the right and flashed a cross-come-shot inches past the far post. But Jimenez had the final say.

Andre located Kieran Trippier, and he moved the ball on for Tommy Doyle to find the Mexican striker, who swept home the decisive goal.

The key moments from Bramall Lane

19: CHANCE ! Rodrigo Gomes flashes in a cross to Marshall Munetsi, whose powerful first-time shot is straight at Michael Cooper.

! Rodrigo Gomes flashes in a cross to Marshall Munetsi, whose powerful first-time shot is straight at Michael Cooper. 50: NO PENALTY ! Mateus Mane flicks the ball towards goal - and it hits the outstretched hand of Mark McGuinness, but referee Rob Jones signals for a corner.

! Mateus Mane flicks the ball towards goal - and it hits the outstretched hand of Mark McGuinness, but referee Rob Jones signals for a corner. 55: WIDE ! Hugo Bueno seizes on a loose ball and shoots from the edge of the box, with the curl taking his effort narrowly past the right-hand post.

! Hugo Bueno seizes on a loose ball and shoots from the edge of the box, with the curl taking his effort narrowly past the right-hand post. 60: Ladislav Krejci pulls Sydie Peck to ground, but avoids a second booking.

67: CLOSE ! Blades debutant Jordan Ayew flashes a shot across the face of goal and just past the post.

! Blades debutant Jordan Ayew flashes a shot across the face of goal and just past the post. 90: GOAL! Raul Jimenez sweeps in the winner from close range to send the away fans wild.

Wilder: Top-end Championship teams can punish you if you switch off

Sheffield United manager Chris Wilder speaking to Sky Sports:

"It's top-end Championship football when you're playing teams like we have done today. They punish you if you just switch off for a moment.

"The players maybe didn't get what they deserved from the game, but that's how the Championship is at times, so we have to roll with that and handle it.

"Especially in the second half, we limited a very attacking team to virtually nothing. I don't think Michael [Cooper] had a save to make.

"It's just disappointing, with the positions we've got into, that we've not found that little bit of quality to get our noses in front."

Peixoto: Subs were important for Wolves - Jimenez is key for us

Wolves head coach Cesar Peixoto speaking to Sky Sports:

"It's an important win for us. We knew it was going to be difficult to play in this stadium against this team. Today, the team was a team for 90 minutes. It was important the guys who came from the bench pushed in the last minutes to try to score. We scored and we won.

"I think we deserved it because we were the better team, but it was a difficult game for us."

On Jimenez: "He's 35 years old, so we have to manage him the best way. He's a key player for us. This week, we have three games, so we had to manage the options. Raul, as a captain, helped the team from the bench, not only with the goal he scored, but he helped to defend the set-pieces."

Sports.title: Rangers thump Celtic to reach League Cup semi-finals
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes won his first Old Firm game as Rangers manager with an utterly dominant 3-0 victory over rivals Celtic to advance to the last four of the Scottish League Cup.

Captain Dan Neil notched a double and £9.2m Deadline Day signing Kevin Kelsy was also on the scoresheet on his Old Firm debut at a rapturous Ibrox Stadium - without the presence of away supporters.

Visitors Celtic struggled to cope with Rangers' aggressive man-for-man press - failing to create any distinct opportunities as they lost a first cup tie in seven against their Glasgow rivals.

Image: Captain Dan Neil bagged his first and second goals as a Rangers player

Kelsy and Minsu Kim both passed up big early opportunities before Neil eventually fired McInnes's side in front after 23 minutes.

The stand-in skipper calmly slotted the ball into the bottom corner with precision from the edge of the area following some great movement and link-up play involving the Rangers' front two of Ryan Naderi and Kelsy.

The Venezuela international then got his first goal for his new club in the second period as he volleyed in Naderi's flick-on at the back post.

Neil completed the scoring with 15 minutes to play as he dispatched the ball into the top corner from the edge of the box to score his second of the afternoon.

Rangers will now face Aberdeen in the semi-finals on the weekend of October 31/November 1, with Hearts drawn against Hibernian.

Key moments from Ibrox

4: RANGERS SHOULD BE IN FRONT! Johnstone tries to clear the ball but sends it straight to Kelsy. With the keeper off his line, he takes aim but it's wide of the post.

16: OFF THE LINE! Another mistake from Johnstone. The goalkeeper slaps the ball to clear, it goes as far as Minsu. He gets a shot away but Scales is there to clear it off the line.

23: RANGERS GOAL! The hosts take the lead and it's what they deserve. Carter-Vickers fails to clear the danger and Kelsy sends the ball to Neil on the edge of the box to fire into the net.

49: SAVE! A big stop from Johnstone! Rangers with the first chance of the second half, Minsu's effort is pushed clear by the Hoops keeper.

50: SAVE! Rangers go close again. Naderi's close-range header is stopped by Johnstone.

59: RANGERS GOAL! Rangers double their lead as Ibrox bursts back into life. Kelsy makes up for his first-half miss and he smashes Penrice's cross into the net for his first Rangers goal.

64: OFFSIDE GOAL! Raskin got the last touch as Fernandez looked to head in from Penrice. Celtic are all over the place.

72: OVER! Celtic get forward only for Hassan to send his effort over the bar.

76: RANGERS GOAL! Wow! The captain Neil with his second of the afternoon. A curling effort into the top corner and Rangers are all but through to that semi-final draw.

McInnes' perfect game plan

Image: Rangers manager Derek McInnes celebrates at full-time

Sky Sports News' Adam Binnie at Ibrox:

Derek McInnes got his game plan spot on.

He used left-back James Penrice as an auxiliary midfielder to flood the middle of the pitch - allowing Rangers to press Celtic man-for-man.

Djeidi Gassama and Minsu Kim provided width and energy as wing-backs with Dujon Sterling, Emmanuel Fernandez and Olewthu Makanya defending three-vs-three against Celtic's front line.

It was a bold decision that paid dividends as Celtic folded under the pressure.

Dan Neil snatched the starring role of midfield general from his Celtic counterpart Callum McGregor, who was left isolated without a defensive-minded midfield partner.

McInnes's side now must face the daunting task of a trip to the home of their rivals with no travelling support next Sunday - live on Sky Sports in the Scottish Premiership.

Win that, and the gap is just two points.

What's coming up...

Sports.title: Leeds Rhinos make up majority of 2026 Super League Dream Team

The Dream Team was selected through three elements, combining the views of the Man of Steel panel (50% per cent), a selected group of Rugby League journalists (30 per cent), and Super League fans (20%).

The conclusion of the vote saw six Leeds players chosen along with two Wigan Warriors players, two Leigh Leopards players, plus a player each from Wakefield Trinity, Warrington Wolves, and Toulouse Olympique.

Such low representation for the Warriors may come as a surprise given that they have already wrapped up a domestic double and are on the hunt for the treble if they reach the Grand Final.

Fullback: Lachie Miller (Leeds Rhinos)

Miller has lit up Super League in 2026, really hitting his stride in the fullback position.

He was top of the Man of Steel standings for the opening nine rounds and was right in the mix for the second third of the season too.

Unfortunately, Miller has suffered a season-ending hamstring injury, which will leave all fans wondering just how much influence he could have had for Leeds in the play-offs.

His link-ups with his half-backs have been electrifying to watch and his pace means he is a mean feat to stop in broken play.

Wigan's Jai Field has also been strong in the fullback role, but in 2026, Miller has been chosen as the competition's most consistent.

Wingers: Maika Sivo (Leeds Rhinos) and Zack Eckersley (Wigan Warriors)

On the wings, we have a try-scoring phenom and a youngster who has had a year to remember in which his career has truly been set alight.

Before suffering his forearm injury at the end of July in round 20, Maika Sivo was scoring at a freakish rate and finishes as Super League's top try scorer with 29 tries.

It is a symbol in itself that he missed six rounds of action and still finished top.

He has 27 tries to his name, just two less than Sivo, but has developed into a winger that Wigan can truly rely on in all facets of their game.

Centres: Ash Handley (Leeds Rhinos) and Umyla Hanley (Leigh Leopards)

In the centres, Ash Handley and Umyla Hanley take the spoils.

Hanley has played just 16 games this season, but since coming back from his injury has been in unbelievable form, which has earned him a call-up to the England squad ahead of the World Cup.

Adam Keighran of the Warriors has also been in great form in that same spot but it is the Leigh man who has shone and earned back-to-back inclusions in the Dream Team.

His head coach Adrian Lam described him as the most "fierce" competitor he has met and he has shown that in spades.

Handley has been the dominant force in the centres for the majority of the season.

The captain of the Rhinos, with his sheer dominance and power, coupled with his speed, has been very hard to stop in 2026.

Stand off: Brodie Croft (Leeds Rhinos)

We said that the Leeds spine has been particularly interwoven in 2026 and that sees Brodie Croft included at stand off.

Remarkably, Croft finishes in second place for try scorers with 28, just one behind his winger Sivo.

He has been there, popping up at every opportunity to get points on the board for his side and makes a return to the Dream Team for the first time in four years.

Scrum half: Jake Connor (Leeds Rhinos)

And the final piece of that Leeds spine puzzle- reigning Man of Steel Jake Connor. He has been the man with all the assists in 2026 and it is back-to-back inclusions for him too.

Connor provided 43 assists across the season. To put into perspective how remarkable a stat that is, second-placed Jackson Hastings provided 29- 14 less than the leader.

His kicking game has also been pivotal for Leeds across this year and now he will want to turn that consistency into big game action.

It is worth a word here for Harry Smith, who has had a really strong year and was also a notable candidate at scrum half.

Hooker: Brad O'Neill (Wigan Warriors)

His defensive efforts are second to none; his aggression has become much more measured, and he has cemented himself as the standout hooker across the year.

Wakefield's Tyson Smoothy has also impressed in the role but O'Neill has been the general in a well-oiled machine and it is the mark of an exceptional player that a team's performance dips when he is not on the field.

Called up to the England squad ahead of the World Cup, Hamlin-Uele has been a stalwart in defence but also given his side go forward when it mattered.

The same can be said of Joe Ofahengaue, who has been arguably Leigh's best player across the year. His gains for his team are right at the top and not only that, he provides an offload threat that means the attack never feels over when he has the ball in hand.

Back Row: James McDonnell (Leeds Rhinos) and Mathieu Jussaume (Toulouse Olympique)

Sports.title: Touleen faces Forty Years On at Doncaster
Sports.content:
The final day of the St Leger Festival sees Touleen clash with Forty Years On.

3.05 Doncaster - Classy fillies Forty Years On and Touleen do battle

The feature on the final day of the Betfred St Leger Festival sees top fillies Forty Years On and Touleen do battle in the Group 3 Japan Racing Association Sceptre Fillies' Stakes.

Touleen tops the ratings for Owen Burrows and new pilot David Probert. She has shown top-class form on her day but has been beaten the last twice including in this grade. Her trainer has enlisted cheekpieces as she seeks a first stakes success, having been arguably unlucky when beaten by Precise in the Coronation Stakes earlier this term.

George Scott's Forty Years On has a rapidly progressive profile having scored on her last two starts and, given the impression she made over course and distance last time, she must be feared in this hotter heat.

Plenty have each-way claims including Darnation and The Prettiest Star, whilst the 102-rated Magic Basma will look to regain the winning thread having not tasted success since her debut win thirteen starts ago.

2.30 Doncaster - Wechaad and Military Code contest excellent handicap

A strong edition of this Betfred City Of Doncaster Handicap sees Wechaad go to post, who will be popular for the Roger Varian team.

A winner over this course and distance last season, this son of Oasis Dream has run a few fair races in defeat and looks to be building to a better effort. Third off this mark at Newmarket, it is hoped he can step forward at a track that suits.

Military Code tops the weights with Toby Moore claiming a handy 7lb in the Godolphin blue. A useful two-year-old, he is yet to score this season but showed improved form in the hood last time and has been dropped another 1lb.

Langstone has good form here, while Zooming and last-time winner Lion Of Mali appeal as best of the rest.

3.40 Doncaster - Valedictory and Say What You See feature

An open feel to this Betfred Mallard handicap sees Valedictory and Say What You See feature among a field of nine.

The John and Thady Gosden-trained Valedictory has been a consistent performer this summer, winning two of his six outings. Having been a tad disappointing at York, connections pop a visor on him this afternoon.

Say What You See heads the opposition for Liam Bailey and Billy Garritty. The son of Belardo remains on the upgrade after another excellent effort at York and a similar run would put him in the mix.

Of the others, Ernst Blofeld has always hinted at better, while All In You is lightly raced in this sphere.

Best of the rest...

Also on Town Moor, a nice-looking Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' Handicap (1.55pm) is headlined by Asuka, who is sure to be fancied for the George Boughey and Billy Loughnane combination. In opposition is Completely Random, who ran a solid race when fourth in the Stewards' Cup but has been hiked up 2lbs to 104 for the effort.

At Bath, Dark Sun and Geemann face off in the 3.50pm Loud Hire Production Services Bath Summer Sprint Series Final Handicap, after Boilermaker headlines proceedings in the 3.15pm Loud Hire Staging Hire Bath Summer Stayers' Series Final Handicap.

Across the channel, Francis-Henri Graffard's Rayevka looks the star in the Prix du Petit Couvert (1.33pm) before attention turns to the Prix du Pin (2.50pm) and Prix du Prince D'Orange (3.25pm) - which sees Daryzan take on Phineas.

Sports.title: Manchester United v Manchester City: Premier League – live
Sports.content:
3m ago 10.38 EDT Will Unwin Enzo Maresca has backed Elliot Anderson’s assessment that ­Manchester City are the “kings of Manchester” as he prepares for his first derby in charge of the club. City travel to Old Trafford seeking to continue their perfect start to life under Maresca and further prove Anderson’s point. The 23-year-old midfielder made his claim on signing from Nottingham Forest for £116m in the summer and having witnessed City win eight Premier League titles during the past 14 years, compared with United’s one. “I think Manchester City was unbelievable what they achieved. It’s normal when Elliot said that,” said Maresca. “If you go back it’s a different picture, but for me the reason he said that is because when he grew up Manchester City was dominant.” Maresca backs Anderson over ‘kings of Manchester’ dig before derby clash Read more Share

8m ago 10.34 EDT Premier League latest: Coventry 0-3 Brighton “Feel free to just gloss over the other game today,” writes Eddy Nason. “Clearly nothing happening there (uncovers eyes to check how bad it’s getting).” Yeah sorry, I’m not sure why we’re not covering that. But it’s a case of grim and grimmer for Coventry fans: their team are 3-0 down after 76 minutes and Taiwo Awoniyi has been sent off. Share

14m ago 10.28 EDT David Hytner It was a sight the England press pack became increasingly used to seeing after the team’s World Cup matches over the summer. Kobbie Mainoo was invariably the first to leave the dressing room, walk through the mixed zone – eyes dead ahead, features impassive – and board the bus. It was as if he could not get out of the stadiums quick enough and the further England progressed the more pronounced it started to feel. There was a real gap between Mainoo and the next England player to depart the stadium in the knockout rounds. The Manchester United midfielder is inscrutable, even in the heat of battle. It is part of his enviably unflappable temperament. It was no great leap to imagine what lay behind the mask – tremendous frustration as Thomas Tuchel kept on leaving him out. Mainoo did not play a single minute at the tournament. He was an unused substitute all the way to the semi-final exit against Argentina, and when everyone expected to see him in the third-place playoff against France he did not make the bench. The Football Association said before the game he had picked up an unspecified injury. For Mainoo it was a lost summer and yet it was physically and mentally draining all the same, what with the training and travel; the demand to stay focused as he waited and waited. . Kobbie Mainoo moves from outsider to main man after summer of hurt Read more Share

16m ago 10.25 EDT Team news United are without Luke Shaw, who has an unspecified injury, so Patrick Dorgu starts at left-back. So much for Michael Carrick repeating his tactics from the win over City in January; on that day Dorgu started as the left-sided attacker and scored the second goal. Dorgu for Shaw is the only change from United’s last Premier League game, the 2-2 draw with Everton a week ago. Enzo Maresca makes two changes from Manchester City’s win over Coventry last weekend. Matheus Nunes replaces Abdukodir Khusanov at right-back; Phil Foden is preferred to Iliman Ndiaye in attack, which may mean a switch from right to left for Antoine Semenyo. The usual left-winger, Jeremy Doku, is still out with a calf injury. Man Utd (4-2-3-1) Lammens; Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Dorgu; Tielemans, Mainoo; Mbeumo, B Fernandes, Rashford; Cunha. Subs: Andrey Santos, Darlow, Heaven, Lacey, Mazraoui, Mount, Sesko, Yoro, Zirkzee. Man City (4-2-3-1) Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Fernandez; Foden, Cherki, Semenyo; Haaland Subs: Rulli, Ndiaye, Kovacic, Reis, Bouaddi, O’Reilly, Allan, Khusanov, Lewis. Referee Michael Oliver. Share Updated at 10.26 EDT

30m ago 10.11 EDT Will Unwin Manchester City have enjoyed a perfect start to the season without ever looking fully convincing in their victories. There are certainly more positives than negatives as Enzo Maresca learns more and more about his team. Against Porto they were sloppy for far too long and the midfield continues to look open, so a statement performance against their fiercest rivals would be ideal. The quality to rip open a team that has conceded two in each of their three Premier League outings thus far is there, and if it all finally clicks, then it could be a fine day for City. Michael Carrick is in a not dissimilar position but only has four points to show for United’s indifferent efforts. There is always an underlying pressure for any Manchester United and he faces difficult league games today and next weekend at Fulham before an elongated international break. He can’t afford two defeats because there will be a long silence that will be filled with think pieces on the club because it is impossible to escape the noise at this club. Share

32m ago 10.09 EDT Jamie Jackson Manchester United’s nine victories from 10 Premier League games at Old Trafford in 2026 cast their stadium as a fortress Manchester City aim to ransack on Sunday, to join Leeds in departing with three points during this calendar year. Michael Carrick has overseen the division’s highest home points-per-game return in that span: 2.7, ahead of Arsenal’s 2.27 (from 12 matches) and Manchester City’s 2.25 (11); and his side have scored the most goals: 26, to City’s 23, and the champions’ 20. A United fan group, the 1958, has called for a “peaceful protest” before kick-off, starting at a pub near the stadium, against what it believes is disproportionate action in the club’s drive to eradicate ticket touting. United said on Friday that 685 accounts had been subject to a ban and 464 supporters had received a reduced sanction or final warning. Febrile Manchester derby awaits amid growing rift between United fans and club Read more Share

Sports.title: Chelsea thrash Manchester United in WSL as Lauren James revels in free role
Sports.content:
A swaggering Chelsea cast off any suggestion that they had lost the ability to kill off games, putting five goals past a worryingly lacklustre and lackadaisical Manchester United side.

The match had been talked about as something of a must win for Sonia Bompastor’s side after they were inexplicably held to a 1-1 draw by Aston Villa on the opening weekend, despite a staggering domination of that match. Criticism felt harsh given their level of control over the game, but signs of the profligacy evident last season reared its head in warning at Stamford Bridge.

To some extent the concern did not need to be too deep. Chelsea were at their creative best against Villa and were without the injured centre-forwards Melvine Malard and Mayra Ramírez, while Aggie Beever-Jones, who led the line against the Midlands side, had not scored in the Women’s Super League since September 2025. Off-target Beever-Jones was relegated to the bench for the trip to United. Instead, Lauren James and Sjoeke Nüsken worked away interchangeably up front.

The visitors were similarly fluid in other areas, lining up for kick-off in a back three, at times converting to a back four and at others seemingly playing with a back two. It was super effective. Chelsea were unpredictable and James’s free-to-roam role put their super-talent at the centre of everything.

Reward for their efforts arrived in the 21st minute. Lucy Bronze sent a looping ball over the top and Dominique Janssen should have been first to it, but the United defender misread the fall of the ball and a stalking Wieke Kaptein nipped it away from her. Kaptein squared to Nüsken who fired in from close-range.

The second goal, which eluded them against Villa, arrived just over 10 minutes later, to stretch the game away from struggling United, who underwhelmed in their 2-1 loss to London City Lionesses in the opening game of the new season. A diving header from new recruit Andrea Medina cleared a cross whipped in from the left but gut-busting Bronze was there to meet it, clipping it into the path of Keira Walsh who took a step and powered in from the edge of the box.

Worryingly, barring a tame early effort from Julia Zigiotti Olme that was easy for Hannah Hampton, United did not threaten at any point, and with their bench light after a heavily criticised summer transfer window, it was difficult to see where any serious threat would arrive from.

A very brief brighter spell after the break was snuffed out by the visiting team. James finally got on the scoresheet after the hour mark, latching on to Walsh’s defence-splitting pass and shrugging off Janssen before sending a low drive in to the net. It was the formidable player’s seventh shot of the game, having twice been denied by superb saves from a full-stretch Phallon Tullis-Joyce.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea’s fourth rubbed salt in for a very wounded United side. Janssen, under no pressure, failed to respond to an ambitious burst from Kaptein and the Chelsea midfielder pickpocketed the centre-back and slipped the ball wide to the onrushing Ellie Carpenter. The Australian’s first effort was kept out by Tullis-Joyce but she could not keep out Carpenter’s follow-up which was blasted emphatically in to the roof of the net. And Bronze poured on some vinegar during the final minute of added time, hammering the ball in after Walsh knocked a corner back into the melee in the six-yard box.

It became a training exercise for the visiting team and the hosts failed in their attempts to limit the damage. Things look as if they will get worse for Eva Olid’s side before they get better, with a trip to the Emirates to play Arsenal coming up next weekend.

Sports.title: Rangers lay down Old Firm marker as Celtic sent packing from Scottish League Cup
Sports.content:
Derek McInnes has endured a much‑scrutinised start to life at Ibrox but the new Rangers manager got the old ground bouncing here as his side dominated Celtic in front of an all-blue crowd to decide the first Old Firm encounter of the season.

Against a backdrop of bouncing techno from the tannoy, Rangers fans celebrated three memorable goals in a thumping League Cup win. A brace for the captain, Dan Neil, bookended Kevin ­Kelsy’s second‑half finish to put Martin O’Neill’s side down with relative ease. It also showcased a nascent identity for McInnes’s side, one defined by unbending physical commitment and lots and lots of sprinting. The quality of the football may have been patchy, but the commitment was enough to get the 51,212 home fans at the top of their voices.

With away fans banned from Old Firm fixtures this season after the pitch invasion that followed a ­Scottish Cup tie last term, the atmosphere was always likely to be partisan, if perhaps less heated than is customary. Before the match there was a brisk trade on both Graeme Souness flags and boiled sweets. Inside the ground the Union Bears ultras unveiled a tifo showcasing the apparently resonant moment when Rangers’ Ian Ferguson grabbed Celtic’s Mike Galloway by the lapels during a clash in 1993. A deep cut of a banner, it did a good job of setting the tone for what was to follow.

McInnes said: “I’m delighted. The performance we gave today was the one required to overcome a team like Celtic. I thought the game demanded the players’ full attention and I’m delighted they’ve managed to deliver that. We’ve seen the strength of the club today and it does the ­players no harm to understand what this match means to so many people.”

Rangers went about the match with an intensity that Celtic ­struggled to equal from the off, some of their ­players looking distinctly overawed by the occasion. The former England goalkeeper Sam Johnstone was among them, flapping at two early openings, but he could do nothing about the ­opening goal when it arrived in the 22nd ­minute. After a Celtic counter broke down Rangers immediately turned play around with a long ball to the Celtic area where Cameron Carter‑Vickers failed to properly clear. Kelsy picked up the loose ball, slipped it to Neil and the captain, signed on a free transfer from Sunderland in the summer, placed an excellent shot just inside ­Johnstone’s left‑hand post.

After seizing the advantage, ­Rangers went on to dominate the ­second half and a second goal appeared inevitable. It duly arrived when a free-kick from the impressive James Penrice was flicked on by Ryan Naderi to the back post where Kelsy clipped his effort around the keeper and inside the left-hand post.

View image in fullscreen Kevin Kelsy lashes in Rangers’ second goal around the hour. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Neil then took matters into his own hands with a quarter of an hour remaining as he controlled a loose ball on the edge of the Celtic area and wrapped a shot into the top corner to unleash delirium in the Copland stand. “I haven’t scored many goals in my career, so to come away with a brace is immense,” Neil said.

It was perhaps just as well for O’Neill that his supporters had been denied access to this match. Celtic began with a calmness that suggested confidence. Ultimately it was more likely to have reflected timidity. The Bhoys were unable to get a foot on the ball at all in the second half, and the big-money signing Kasper Høgh looked lost at the tip of the Celtic attack before he was substituted on 65 minutes.

“We were well beaten in the end, on the day we were second best,” O’Neill said afterwards. “There has to be a realisation how big this game is, it’s still one of the great ­fixtures in European football if not the world. We’ve got to know that. We have to learn from it. Hopefully it’s a wake‑up call.”

Rangers will play Aberdeen in the semi-finals, but McInnes was still being asked about Rangers’ stuttering start to the season after this match, generating the timeless response: “Why are you pissing on my chips?”

After this result the Rangers mana­ger can at least look forward with optimism and he could be set to unleash the spirit of Ian Ferguson again as early as next weekend when a second Old Firm derby awaits, this time at Celtic Park.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta says penalty given to Sunderland ‘unacceptable at this level’
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta’s delight at Arsenal’s latest win was tempered by his fury with the referee John Brooks as the champions triumphed 2-0 at Sunderland on Saturday night.

Before Bruno Guimarães gave Arsenal the lead in a tight match that Régis Le Bris’s team were arguably unlucky to lose, David Raya made a brilliant save to deny Enzo Le Fée from the penalty spot. Arteta, however, did not believe that Ezri Konsa had hauled Dan Ballard to the ground, instead blaming the Sunderland man for pulling down his opponent.

“We had to overcome a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” said Arsenal’s manager. “Sunderland can suffocate you and they decided to be really physical and very direct and we also had to overcome a situation that, in my opinion was unacceptable at this level.

“I’m very worried and sad because this can never be a penalty. It’s a judo roll from the opponent. Ezri does nothing. We have to take responsibility to protect the game. Today the game was unprotected and it could have cost us the win and our momentum. I’m really sad. It should never have happened.”

Arteta, who was booked in the first half for persistently stepping out of his technical area, hailed Guimarães’s goal as “beautiful” after watching Bukayo Saka scored a second goal from the penalty spot in stoppage time, when Sunderland’s Reinildo was sent off for a second bookable offence.

Le Bris was left with mixed feelings. “I’m proud and disappointed, these are the two words that are in my mind at the minute,” said Sunderland’s manager. “I’m proud because I think we showed that we are really close to achieving something big against one of the best teams in Europe right now. After the first half we were a bit reserved with the ball I think, but our second half was excellent.

“We got the momentum, created chances and it was a big save from Raya from the penalty. I think it was very good goalkeeping rather than a poor penalty. Raya was absolutely impressive today.

“We stayed in the game and we created other chances but we didn’t score and that was the difference today.

Today we found a solution to stop them and we created chances as well so it shows that we are getting better. It’s not enough yet but we are close.”

Sports.title: Spygate saga continues to haunt Southampton as case drags on
Sports.content:
Fifty seconds was all it took for the chant to begin. “You know what you are, you know what you are, cheating bastards, you know what you are,” bellowed the Bristol City fans, starting up a cry heard from every away contingent coming to St Mary’s Stadium this season. The Southampton supporters responded with sarcastic applause, then drowned out the noise with songs of their own.

This is what life is now like for Southampton after May’s spying scandal – a saga whose full consequences are still unknown and could have ramifications for the season ahead. The English Football League acted swiftly after photographs emerged of a junior staff member hiding behind a tree to film a Middlesbrough training session, expelling Southampton from the Championship play-offs and deducting four points after the club admitted multiple spying offences, including on Oxford United and Ipswich. The Football Association’s case against Tonda Eckert, the manager, is taking far longer. And patience is wearing thin.

The incident left a deep stain on Southampton’s reputation, one that will take time to fade and will leave an indelible mark on their history. Fans initially felt a mixture of fury and embarrassment – their promotion hopes snatched away over smartphone footage of a rival’s training session. Still, it has not stopped them flocking to St Mary’s this season: attendances were a shade under 30,000 for visits from Stoke, Millwall and Swansea and a season-high of 30,132 made Saturday’s Bristol City match almost a sell-out.

“Initially I was disappointed and angry,” says Alex Watson, a 31-year-old Saints fan, outside the stadium before kick-off. “Then you go through all the stages up to acceptance.”

Frustration is now turning towards the FA for taking so long to confirm what punishment – if any – Eckert will face after being charged individually by the governing body. A fine or short ban would be manageable. But Bev Priestman was banned for a year by Fifa, while manager of Canada, after two staff members used a drone to spy on an opponent at the Paris Olympics, so there is precedent for a lengthy suspension. That would likely see Eckert be removed as manager.

It is nearly two months since the FA charged Eckert with misconduct, even though the EFL’s independent panel took a matter of days to determine Eckert authorised the spying and that it was a “contrived and determined plan from the top down”.

“The mood generally is the FA needs to make a decision,” Watson says. “They need to get on and do something about it, one way or the other.”

There is a lingering sense of inconsistency between sanctions for big clubs and the rest – an irritation shared across the country. Chelsea received fines and suspended transfer bans from the Premier League and FA for systemic breaches of agent rules between 2009 and 2022. Yet Southampton have been kicked out of a competition, docked four points and may lose their manager for filming some training sessions.

If anything, Southampton fans have begun leaning into the pantomime-villain role. On the hour, a chant of “We spy when we want, we spy when we want, we are Southampton, we spy when we want” broke out. Within a minute, Cyle Larin had put them two in front with his second of the match.

View image in fullscreen Cyle Larin scores to put Southampton 2-0 up against Bristol City. Photograph: Matt Watson/Southampton FC/Getty Images

While awaiting a verdict, the club have been preparing for all eventualities. During a preseason friendly against Preussen Münster, Eckert watched from the stands while his assistant, Ben Garner, took charge in the dugout – practising how operations might work if the German is handed a touchline ban.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The scandal did not deter summer signings. The goalkeeper Daniel Peretz was a £6m coup from Bayern Munich, agreeing to make his loan permanent after playing through the storm. Larin made a similar commitment and the Canadian forward has scored eight goals in nine games. The fan favourite James Ward-Prowse, a star of their last Premier League spell, decided to return.

Early indications are that the team can be promotion challengers. Late goals from Kuryu Matsuki and Finn Azaz completed a thumping win. After the final whistle, Eckert walked around the Northam and the Itchen Stands applauding; the fans stood to applaud back. Eckert, who returned after the summer uncertain how fans would react, says their backing “means everything” to him.

Asked if he has found it easy to block out the looming FA decision, he said: “I wouldn’t call it easy. But life isn’t always easy, if you have big goals then you need to find a way.” He added: “The fans have every right to react differently to the situation, how it’s evolved over the last season. I would’ve respected every reaction and decision from the club, the board and the supporters. Either you can forgive or you can’t. That’s not my decision. It’s just to accept how the reaction is.”

Had Southampton not started the season with a four-point deduction, they would be level on points with the top of the table. Losing the manager behind it would be another cruel twist.

Sports.title: De Zerbi says Spurs have ‘mental block’ after wait for league win continues
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi says his Tottenham players continue to lack physical fitness and must “unblock” themselves in psychological terms after they drew their latest Premier League blank in a home 0-0 with Everton. It is now four games in the competition since the start of the season without a goal for Spurs; they sit 17th in the table with two points and were booed off by frustrated fans.

De Zerbi gave a number of explanations for Spurs’ slow start, chief among them the injuries that a clutch of players sustained on the long-haul pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia. He lamented the impact of the World Cup on the return dates of certain players and mentioned how Sávio and Omar Marmoush had signed late in the transfer window.

De Zerbi talked up a positive opening 30 minutes from his players against Everton but accepted they ran out of steam and that there was a psychological problem.

“There is a word in Italian – sbloccarsi – that literally translates as if we unblock ourselves,” De Zerbi said. “[It is] a mental block because four games, no wins, no goals scored … it is tough for the players. The team is extremely strong, we can score goals and we can win games. And then we have to respect the history of the players in their careers. Forget Dominic Solanke and Marmoush – the other players … they didn’t score many, many goals in their careers and we have to find these goals. I think we can do so with the quality of our play.”

De Zerbi warmed to a familiar theme when he went back to the pre-season tour. “I said we started this season late for many, many reasons; too late,” he said. “Many players at the World Cup, many injuries, many problems in Australia. Micky van de Ven suffered an injury in Australia. Domi Solanke the same. James Maddison the same. Mateus Fernandes suffered an injury in Australia. He lost 15 days and it’s not so quick. Sávio and Marmoush, they came 10 days ago. I started to work with this [whole] group not last Thursday but two Thursdays ago. So, I think we have not the right physical condition yet.

“We played very well in the first 30 minutes and then maybe the energy, maybe the fact we didn’t score … maybe we lost in some players a little confidence. We have to be not positive but realistic.
