“If we extend that part of the game to 60, 70, 80 and 90 minutes, in my opinion, we are going to win many games. We have to improve in the last third of the pitch, for sure. The last decision, the last pass and we have to shoot more times, especially when we have space and time. But I can’t say nothing bad about the players.”

Sports.title: European football: Dortmund win again but Freiburg top after Gladbach rout
Sports.content:
Felix Nmecha scored twice and Fábio Silva grabbed another as Borussia Dortmund won 3-0 at home to promoted Paderborn to continue their perfect start in the Bundesliga. Dortmund’s win made it three from three in the league this campaign, their best start in 11 seasons, dating back to Thomas Tuchel’s time.

Starting up front alongside Serhou Guirassy for the first time this season, Silva converted a clever pass from the Guinean to give the hosts the lead after five minutes. Guirassy had two goals disallowed for offside in the first half but Dortmund were rarely troubled by the toothless visitors, who are yet to score since returning to the top flight.

Nmecha came off the bench to score twice, wrapping up victory for the hosts with a stunning late bicycle kick.

Dortmund captain Nico Schlotterbeck made his first appearance since picking up an ankle injury at the World Cup and told Sky Germany he kept his comeback under wraps. “We just hadn’t communicated that much yet because I didn’t want to,” Schlotterbeck said, adding “I missed it terribly. It was a serious injury but I’m glad to be back now.”

Freiburg thumped a poor Borussia Mönchengladbach 5-0 at home to climb to the top. Yannik Engelhardt and Igor Matanovic netted twice each and Maximilian Eggestein added a late fifth as the hosts sent Gladbach, who finished with 10 men, to the foot of the table.

View image in fullscreen Freiburg’s Matthias Ginter (centre) congratulates Igor Matanovic on the opening goal against Borussia Mönchengladbach. Photograph: Philipp von Ditfurth/DPA/AP

A 2-2 home draw with Bayer Leverkusen ended Augsburg’s short stint as leaders. Augsburg were top after the last matchday for the first time in their history but were held by Leverkusen despite a double from Michael Gregoritsch.

Eintracht Frankfurt won their first match of the campaign with a 3-1 victory at neighbouring Mainz, with Can Uzun’s double either side of a Jonathan Burkardt goal. Frankfurt’s goalkeeper Noah Atubolu kept his remarkable penalty-saving record alive when he stopped a first-half effort from Nadiem Amiri. Atubolu’s save was his sixth in a row, extending his own Bundesliga record.

West Ham loanee Niclas Füllkrug kept his excellent run of form since returning to the Bundesliga going, scoring the equaliser for Werder Bremen in a 1-1 draw at Cologne. Thijs Dallinga missed a penalty after eight minutes but teammate Linton Maina put Cologne ahead moments later.

Füllkrug’s goal came in the 69th minute and is his third in four games since returning to Germany. He only found the net three times in 29 matches for West Ham and scored just once in 20 games on loan at Milan last season.

Elsewhere, Hoffenheim won 2-1 at home against Stuttgart thanks to a double from Adam Hlozek. On Sunday, Bayern Munich travel to promoted Elversberg – who have a 100% record – while RB Leipzig host Hamburg.

In Spain, Kylian Mbappé scored twice ⁠as Real Madrid enjoyed a 4-1 victory over Rayo Vallecano ⁠in La Liga ⁠at ​the Santiago Bernabéu. Goals from Álvaro Carreras and Jude ⁠Bellingham made the result comfortable for José Mourinho’s side.

View image in fullscreen Kylian Mbappé celebrates scoring Real’s fourth against Rayo Vallecano. Photograph: Manu Fernández/AP

A 14th-minute ⁠penalty from Mbappé was followed three minutes ​later by ‌a simple finish ‌from Carreras, with Mbappé turned provider ‌this time. A relaxed Real found little resistance from Rayo thereafter and, 11 minutes before half time, Vinícius Júnior raced down the left to set up ‌Bellingham for a neat finish into the corner.

Six minutes into the ​second half, Sergio Camello pulled a goal back for Rayo following sloppy Real Madrid play. Despite whistles from the ⁠home crowd, Real kept Rayo at ​bay, ​before closing out the ​game with a 90th-minute goal ​from ‌Mbappé.

The result ​moved ​Real on to 12 points, level with leaders Barcelona, who have a game in hand. Barça are at Levante on Sunday afternoon. Alavés missed the chance to go top overnight with a 2-1 defeat at Racing Santander.

In Italy, Diego Moreira scored twice as Milan came from two goals down to hold early season Serie A pacesetters Lazio 2-2 in Rome on Saturday. Moreira came off the bench at half-time and hauled Milan level after Matteo Cancellieri and Tijjani Noslin had given the hosts the lead at the interval.

Despite losing their 100% record having started the season with three wins, Gennaro Gattuso’s side move to the top of the table. Ruben Amorim’s Milan are fourth on eight points, after also drawing last weekend at Juventus.

View image in fullscreen Milan’s Diego Moreira celebrates scoring in his side’s 2-2 draw with Lazio. Photograph: Riccardo Antimiani/EPA

Cancellieri opened his account for the campaign after 10 minutes when he connected with a Mattia Zaccagni cross. A dominant Lazio had good chances to pull further clear before Noslin doubled their lead after 39 minutes with a close-range finish.

Amorim attempted to stem the tide by making three substitutions at half-time, bringing on playmaker Christian Pulisic and Moreira. His changes bore fruit after 65 minutes as Moreira volleyed home to halve the deficit. Less than two minutes later, the former Strasbourg player equalised with a fierce strike from outside the box, but neither side could find a late winner.

Atalanta slumped to a 2-1 defeat at home to Cagliari, with Sead Kolasinac handling the ball in the box to concede a second-half penalty that gave the visitors the win. Cagliari took the lead in the 19th ⁠minute when 19-year-old forward Paul Mendy rattled in the opener off the underside of the crossbar, ​but Gianluca Scamacca levelled for the home side ​four minutes before the break.

Mendy had the ​ball in the net again early in the second half only for the goal to be ruled out ​for a narrow offside, but ‌they took the lead ​again after Kolasinac was penalised, ​Daniel Maldini firing home from the spot to secure the three points.

The result moved Cagliari up to fourth in the table with nine points from their four games, while Atalanta are in ninth spot on six points. Earlier, hosts Genoa, who have yet to win this season, were held 1-1 by newly promoted Frosinone, who have seven points.

Champions Inter host Udinese on Monday, with Roma heading to Torino and Como at home to Parma. Inter and Roma have both won each of their first three matches.

Sports.title: Hull stun Chelsea with Mohamed Belloumi double before João Pedro rescues a point
Sports.content:
The chants from the away end about winning the league were sung in jest, but Hull continue to show they are here to stay. Sergej Jakirovic’s dogged, intelligent side are third in the Premier League after extending their unbeaten start to four games and can even count themselves unfortunate not to have beaten another of the Big Six after pushing Chelsea to the limit in an absorbing battle at a frustrated Stamford Bridge.

Hull were 2-1 up at half-time and they had the chances to snatch the points during the second half. It took two big saves from Emiliano Martínez to prevent an upset, but this was not a good day for the Chelsea goalkeeper or his new teammates. He was one of several at fault when Hull, having dusted themselves down after conceding from Morgan Rogers early on, went ahead through Mohamed Belloumi’s quickfire double. The ease with which Chelsea’s advantage was handed over left the normally calm and considered Xabi Alonso accusing his side of being “soft” without the ball.

Alonso craves the comfort of a forgettable win. Chelsea have been exhilarating in attack, but they cannot defend. They are conceding two goals per game and the basketball nature of Alonso’s approach has created chaos rather than control. “It’s all entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win,” he said. “It will take time. When we get the lead you still need to be competing and not to give the chance so easily for them to come back.

“Especially in the first goal, we can do much better. It was too soft to give them hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances, but that changed the mood. We will get better, but it’s having an impact on our performances.”

It is ridiculous that Rogers, Cole Palmer and João Pedro are having to do so much in attack. Chelsea led after seven minutes, surging forward when they left four players forward at a Hull corner. João Pedro’s pass reached Rogers and the £117m signing from Aston Villa drove past Regan Slater before beating Konstantinos Tzolaki at his near post with a low, hard and early shot from the left.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro fires home Chelsea’s equaliser in the second half. Photograph: Andy Rain/EPA

Chelsea should have pushed on after becoming the first side to breach Hull since their promotion. Pedro Neto tested Tzolakis from the right, but the hosts became vague and complacent. This was the first time they have dominated possession in a league game this season and the result was not convincing. Hull limited them to an xG of 0.89, highlighting Chelsea’s issues against low blocks, and were clinical when they attacked.

The soft defending Alonso referenced for the equaliser started with Malo Gusto failing to deal with a long punt from Tzolakis in the 28th minute. Ryan Giles outmuscled the right-back and hooked a cross to the far post. Jorrel Hato misread the Hull left-back’s delivery, leaving Belloumi to rap a shot past Martínez.

Chelsea are without a win against promoted sides in five home games. They do not smell danger, while Alonso’s decision to leave Maxence Lacroix out at centre-back and shift from a back three to a 4-2-3-1 system backfired. Hull had so much space on the flanks. They pushed again and Belloumi’s flick found Lewie Coyle, who ran off Rogers but saw his shot cleared off the line by Levi Colwill.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“The dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it,” Alonso said. “Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”

There was no response from Chelsea after Colwill turned Coyle’s shot wide. A corner came in from the left, Martínez flapped and Semi Ajayi’s header hit the bar. The ball came to Belloumi, whose shot flew in thanks to a deflection.

Alonso reacted at half-time, Hato making way for Pep Chavarría at left-back. Reece James drew a save from Tzolakis with a free-kick but Hull carried a threat on the break. They almost extended their lead when Martínez spilled a shot from Slater.

Martínez redeemed himself, blocking the rebound from McBurnie, and Chelsea soon levelled. Palmer, otherwise quiet, surprised Hull with a direct run. The No 10 drove down the left and picked out João Pedro, who lashed a shot into the roof of the net.

Hull refused to lie down. Ajayi, Giles and John Egan were outstanding at the back and the visitors maintained their shape when losing Nobel Mendy after a nasty collision with João Pedro.

Jakirovic made bold substitutions. Alonso threw Danny Welbeck on. Palmer scooped over from 20 yards and Tzolakis thwarted Rogers, but Hull had the best chance. Giles crossed again and Mohamed-Ali Cho shot straight at Martínez from close range.

Hull settled for a point. Jakirovic quashed talk of qualifying for Europe, insisting that survival remains the aim. The Bosnian has everyone pulling in the same direction. Before the start of the season he told his staff he would give them seven days off if Hull took eight points from their first five games. Mission completed with a game to spare.

Sports.title: Gareth Southgate set to launch new podcast starring his old England favourite, no love lost between EFL and Southampton after Spygate - and toilet roll troubles continue at Man United's Leigh Sports Village: INSIDE SPORT
Sports.content:
In November, Inside Sport noted how reporters covering Manchester United’s women side when they play at the Leigh Sports Village had taken to bringing their own toilet roll to games thanks to a lack of the product at the council-operated facility.

United have long denied claims of a lack of investment in their women’s team but the noise refuses to go away following the departure of head coach Marc Skinner.

On Sunday, it got louder when they made it back-back losses to open the campaign escaping a lop-sided home clash with Chelsea with a 5-0 pasting while, up in the press box, there was again no loo roll.

Spygate tensions rumble on

As they await the Spygate verdict from the FA, there would appear to be no love lost between Southampton and the EFL. Spies inside the boardroom at Birmingham City have told Inside Sport that EFL chief Rick Parry, who was at St Andrews for the Saints' recent Championship clash, did not speak to any of the travelling delegation, preferring instead to spend the duration of his visit with Blues officials.

The apparent snub did not go unnoticed at Southampton, where there remains some upset about how the decision to throw them out of the play-offs unfolded. While the FA’s punishment remains to be seen, any further measures would no doubt add to that feeling, given the Saints have already paid the ultimate penalty.

EFL insiders say that Parry was in a different area of the boardroom and did not spot the Saints party.

EFL chief Rick Parry, who was at St Andrews for the Saints' recent Championship clash, did not speak to any of the travelling delegation, Inside Sport understands

Chakraborty hard to replace for BBC

Federation bosses are closely monitoring the BBC’s next move ahead of the Olympics following the departure of its head of major events and general sport. Ron Chakraborty is departing the broadcaster at the end of the year after more than 28 years.

He leads the Beeb’s Olympics coverage and, as a highly-respected operator, leaves big shoes to fill. ‘Ron is a great guy,’ explained one source, ‘and did a brilliant job on this year’s Winter Games. It will be interesting to see what they do for LA – producing 35 sports is not easy. There’s nothing like it.’

Some have accused the Beeb, under director of sport Alex Kay-Jelski, of showing little regard for television as it searches for a younger audience by pouring resource into digital output.

Insiders say they are confident in their succession plan, believe in the team that delivered both the summer and winter Games, which remains in place, and say additional leadership oversight will be provided. They reject any suggestion that LA coverage will be compromised given the expertise they believe remains at their disposal.

Southgate set to launch new podcast

Gareth Southgate is set to expand his media empire with a new podcast focusing on managers. Insiders say the show is set to be named The Dugout, and is expected to feature broadcaster Mark Chapman and former Everton defender Conor Coady speaking to bosses from across the game.

Southgate, along with long-time business partner Jimmy Worrall have already launched The Football Boardroom, which aims to take listeners inside the corridors of power.

EFL clubs will meet this week in their divisions to discuss key matters. Inside Sport understands that they will be briefed on the latest with regards to financial distribution, as a deal with the Premier League inches closer.

Gareth Southgate is set to expand his media empire with a new podcast focusing on managers

Russini suffers fresh blow after Vrabel scandal

It would appear that Dianna Russini, the reporter at the centre of a huge NFL scandal, has cast her final vote in the sport’s prestigious end of year awards.

Russini, 43, resigned from her role with The Athletic, in the wake of explosive allegations over her relationship with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel. She was one of 50 journalists selected to make picks in the Associated Press’s poll, holding the coveted spot since 2022.

Russini and Vrabel, who are both married with children, denied having an affair after shock pictures emerged of them together at an adults-only resort in Arizona.

However, the images, coupled with further shots which appeared to show the pair kissing in a New York City bar in 2020 led some to call on the AP to release ballots from previous polls amid concerns over integrity. They have declined to do so.

Inside Sport asked AP to clarify whether Russini would be voting this year. They stopped short of directly answering the question however, in a quote, seemed to suggest that would not be the case.

A spokesperson said simply: ‘The makeup of AP’s NFL awards voting panel changes regularly as sports reporters change positions and organizations, and this year is no different.’

Sports.title: Real Madrid take over the Spanish Grand Prix: Jude Bellingham is joined by his brother Jobe and Trent Alexander-Arnold... while Jose Mouriunho interview with Sky Sports' Martin Brundle is awkwardly cut short
Sports.content:
Real Madrid take over the Spanish Grand Prix: Jude Bellingham is joined by his brother Jobe and Trent Alexander-Arnold... while Jose Mouriunho interview with Sky Sports' Martin Brundle is awkwardly cut short

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jude Bellingham led a cohort of Real Madrid stars in attending the Spanish Grand Prix in the capital, as he declared his support for Mercedes drivers.

Bellingham was joined by his brother Jobe – whose Borussia Dortmund team won 3-0 on Saturday – as Madrid hosted a Formula One race for the first time since 1981.

The brothers were seen in the McLaren garage ahead of the race, while they also stopped off with their rivals Mercedes.

Bellingham was seen embracing drivers' championship leader Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, with Real Madrid players and drivers exchanging signed shirts.

Fede Valverde, Vinicius Jnr, Rodrygo and Trent Alexander-Arnold were also among the current Real Madrid stars present.

The trip followed Real Madrid earning a 4-1 victory over Rayo Vallecano on Saturday night, with Bellingham among the scorers for Jose Mourinho's side.

Jude Bellingham and his brother Jobe were among the sporting stars present for the Madrid Grand Prix

The Bellingham brothers visited both McLaren and Mercedes garages ahead of the race

Jose Mourinho and Trent Alexander-Arnold were also part of a cohort from Real Madrid to attend the race after they had overcome Rayo Vallecano 4-1 on Saturday

'Good going, a good start to the season for the team, one little slip up but other than that doing pretty good,' Bellingham said when asked by Sky Sports about their start to the season.

On the Grand Prix, Bellingham added: 'I have been with Mercedes and met George and Kimi, they have been telling us about it [F1] and I have to act like I understand.

'To be honest the level those guys are operating at with the strategy and all those things is a different level.

'It is unbelievable, I am used to a PlayStation controller but these guys are whipping out things with 40 buttons.

'Credit to them and with the work they put in, they deserve everything they get.

'The thing I most admire is the poise of them all, it is really impressive.'

In a separate interview, Bellingham revealed that he typically cheers on Mercedes and British drivers during the F1 season.

Real Madrid boss Mourinho was also present having vowed only to be in attendance if his side were victorious on Saturday.

Mourinho was seen in dicussion with Spanish tennis legend Rafael Nadal at the Grand Prix

Real Madrid great Roberto Carlos spoke to Fernando Alonso in the Aston Martin garage

Mourinho's interview with Sky Sports' grid reporter Martin Brundle was abruptly halted in an awkward moment for the broadcaster.

Brundle had seconds left of his customary segment, and had to cut off the interview after just a brief exchange, when the national anthem began playing with the drivers assembled and Mourinho mid-sentence.

Mourinho was earlier collared by another Sky Sports reporter trackside where he was asked about whether Bellingham could one day be considered England's greatest player.

'Very special,' Mourinho replied. 'Not a bit special, very special.'

Mourinho, however, offered no prediction when asked about how his former club Man United and coach Michael Carrick will get on in Sunday's Manchester derby.

'He's doing well Michael, doing well, I'm happy with that,' Mourinho said.

Mourinho was also pictured in conversation with legendary Spanish tennis star Rafael Nadal at the Grand Prix.

Former Real Madrid greats Roberto Carlos and Steve McManaman were also among the sporting icons present.

Sports.title: Michael Vaughan insists England must win trophies to justify hiring another 'big vibe personality' as Kevin Pietersen takes on new role as white-ball coach - and admits what surprised him about his 'risky' appointment
Sports.content:
Michael Vaughan says England must win trophies after appointing another 'vibe' coach - but insists they couldn't have got a better one than Kevin Pietersen.

The timing of Pietersen's arrival as a limited overs mentor - he starts work today - is curious, not least because England have won 17 of their most recent 19 completed Twenty20 internationals, briefly occupying the world's No 1 ranking in July, and have begun turning the ship around in the one-day format too, claiming series wins over Sri Lanka and India this year.

Vaughan says of the link-up of his 2005 Ashes team-mate with England's white-ball coach Brendon McCullum: 'I like it, it's quirky. It's a risk, it has to be a risk because you're not too sure what you're going to get because Kev's not done a great deal of coaching.

'But his knowledge of batting, his knowledge of winning, his knowledge of playing at the right intensity at the right moments, there's no-one been better in my time playing for England. He'll add that.

'The intriguing part for me is how this works in terms of the different personalities in the backroom team. England have gone for a very powerful, famous backroom team.

'There are a few backroom teams that are doing really well around the world that I don't even know, just quietly coaching and going about their business.

Kevin Pietersen has begun his new role as a specialist white-ball coach for England

The timing of Pietersen's arrival as a limited overs mentor - he starts work today - is curious

Pietersen will work alongside white-ball coach Brendon McCullum in the England setup

'But England have gone for this and have done under Rob Key for a while now, he likes the big vibe of personality. They've got to start winning trophies, to justify all these decisions and, let's be honest a huge amount of money spent.'

Pietersen, 46, was sacked by England alongside coach Andy Flower in 2014, after multiple fall-outs as a player. So, given the acrimonious past, is Vaughan surprised to see him donning the three lions tracksuit again?

'No, I'm happy he's back in English cricket because 2014 I always felt that Kev was dealt an iffy hand. Kev brings a lot of things on himself but there are many others who have done equally silly things and have been allowed back into English cricket,' he explains.

'I was actually surprised they've brought him into the white-ball set-up. I thought the Test team would have approached him. The white-ball team over the last year have been doing quite well. T20s, No.1 in the world. 50-over team, back on track.

'I would think that he will be having an influence on the batters in the white-ball team who play Test cricket.'

Vaughan - speaking to promote the Barclays Knight-Stokes Cup, the state school competition he hopes to see expand from 1,100 entrants this summer to 2,000 in 2027 - also believes that Ollie Robinson is the bowler Australia will be concerned about facing most in next year's Ashes after his four Test outings this summer yielded 28 wickets at a cost of single figures each.

'It's just so natural for Ollie Robinson. He just runs in and hits that length naturally,' Vaughan suggests.

'I guess we're all sceptical of what it'll look like in the winter when it's a bit hotter (in South Africa) and he gets into his second, third and fourth spells, comes back the next day and bowls with the Kookaburra ball.

'But here in the UK, I wouldn't want to face him. And the Aussies will know next summer they'll have to try and overcome him one of two ways.

'They'll have to have someone who completely nullifies him technically to see him off or you go the risky game which is Travis Head at the top to try and whack him out of his length. I'll be intrigued to see which way they go.

Michael Vaughan believes England must win trophies after appointing another 'big vibe' coach

England prioritising bowling over pitches, says Trescothick Marcus Trescothick says England are more focused on preparing an elite fast bowling pack than sporting pitches ahead of next summer's Ashes. Signing off before the arrival of incoming Test coach Stephen Fleming on Monday, Joe Root's team completed a 3-0 whitewash of Pakistan as a seam attack marshalled by Ollie Robinson - and including the 90 mile per hour speed of Jofra Archer and Josh Tongue - made the Dukes ball talk in bowler-friendly conditions. Few would argue that the surfaces this summer have offered more lateral movement than others of recent vintage, leading to suggestions that Australia should be presented with a similar set in 2027. But interim head coach Trescothick countered: 'Let's not throw it too far ahead. It's done a bit this season. No doubt about it, more than we've seen in previous years. I don't think we're getting anywhere near looking at the Ashes (though) because we've got a really important series in South Africa. 'There's another transition to happen with Stephen coming in and working with Joe and planning how they're going to move things forward from here. So, I think keep it really simple at the moment and just sit back and enjoy what's happened in the last month. 'I'm not judging on conditions. I think as a general rule our bowling attack is coming into a nice place.'

'I like this attack a lot because it's got all the different variables that you need. I think we've got to be a bit wary of bigging them up too much because of what they've bowled against (Pakistan).

'But if they can keep their mentality and fitness and realise the balls they've bowled in this series are going to challenge every batting unit in the world, they will have things covered pretty well.

'If you cover the basics in Test cricket, it just generally gets you into a good position in most games and series.'

England's next Test assignment is against world champions South Africa in their own backyard in December and one of the most pressing planning issues for captain Joe Root to discuss with newly-appointed coach Stephen Fleming when they meet up in person for the first time this week is how the top six accommodates the return of Jacob Bethell from knee surgery.

Jordan Cox and Dan Lawrence both made strong cases to remain in England's first-choice XI against Pakistan, but Vaughan believes Emilio Gay should remain at the top of the order.

'Three 50s in his first six games, and some of the conditions have been pretty tough for batting. I don't think he's completely stamped his name in that first Test in South Africa because to do that you need to get hundreds,' Vaughan reflects.

'One hundred would have probably guaranteed that he played the whole winter. He's looked okay. Looked like he can play at this level, so I'd certainly start with him.

'Other permutations (mean) manoeuvring people out of position. So, that means opening the batting with someone who doesn't open, or hasn't done too much opening the batting.

'Emilio Gay is an opening batter, so I would stay with him for a period. On the South Africa tour, we will find out a lot more about him, a lot more about the team because it's going to be more challenging.'

Thousands of teams

Sports.title: Furious Cristiano Ronaldo calls for lifetime bans after fans target Ruben Neves with disgraceful Diogo Jota chants during Saudi Pro League match
Sports.content:
Furious Cristiano Ronaldo calls for lifetime bans after fans target Ruben Neves with disgraceful Diogo Jota chants during Saudi Pro League match

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Cristiano Ronaldo has furiously called for Saudi Pro League spectators who shamefully taunted Ruben Neves with chants about his late friend Diogo Jota to be handed lifetime bans.

Footage shared on social media showed Neves responding to Al-Taawoun supporters repeatedly chanting Jota's name in the direction of the Portugal and Al-Hilal midfielder on Saturday.

Neves appeared to signal to the fans that 'God is watching', as he pointed first to the sky, then to his eyes and finally in their direction. The Portuguese star could be seen repeating the gesture before returning to the game.

Portugal captain Ronaldo posted on Instagram on Sunday: 'The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behavior. This is no longer football, and there have to be limits. People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again.'

Neves briefly referenced the incident after Al-Hilal recorded a 6-0 victory over Al-Taawoun, as he quickly walked through the mixed zone post-match.

'I hope they don't go to prayer later,' Neves told reporters, appearing to contrast the behaviour of the fans with religious teachings.

Cristiano Ronaldo has furiously called for Saudi Pro League spectators who shamefully taunted Ruben Neves with chants about his late friend Diogo Jota to be handed lifetime bans

Ruben Neves was targeted by groups of Al-Taawoun supporters who chanted the name of his late team-mate Diogo Jota during a Saudi Pro League match on Saturday

Neves appeared to signal to the fans that 'God is watching', as he pointed first to the sky, then to his eyes and finally in their direction

Post-match Neves told reporters 'I hope they don't go to prayer later, appearing to contrast the behaviour of the fans with religious teachings

Neves had been the best friend of the late Liverpool star Jota, who tragically died at the age of 28 alongside his brother Andre Silva, 25, after a car crash in northern Spain in July 2025.

Neves, who played with Jota at Wolves and with Portugal, had been one of the pallbearers at Jota's funeral.

The 29-year-old last year revealed he had a new leg tattoo of him hugging his late team-mate in an emotional tribute, while Portugal decided Neves should wear Jota's No21 shirt.

Neves has also been a constant figure of support for Jota's widow Rute Cardoso, who had married the star just 11 days before the tragic car accident, which took place while he was driving back to the UK for pre-season training.

The chants from Al-Taawoun fans to Jota have been condemned in Saudi Arabia.

Waleed Al-Farraj, a prominent Saudi football broadcaster, claimed the chants lacked 'humanity'.

'For you to say 'Messi' to [Cristiano] Ronaldo, this goes within the competition that exists between them, but to chant at Neves, the Al-Hilal player, with the name of his deceased team-mate Jota, this is an improper act,' Al-Farraj said.

'How do you play on people's sorrows in this way? You must have some humanity.'

Ronaldo demanded the Saudi Pro League take action and punish the culprits with lifetime bans

Jota tragically died at the age of 28 in July last year following a car crash in Spain

Neves and Jota were close friends and played alongside each other on 164 occasions

Neves last year revealed a tattoo on his leg of him embracing his friend in a touching tribute

Saudi Arabian international Saleh Abu Al-Shamat, who plays for Al-Ahli, also labelled the chants as 'wrong and unacceptable' in a social media post.

'I wanted to draw attention to something we all witnessed today. I felt it was my duty - as a Muslim - to share this and raise awareness,' Abu Al-Shamat wrote on Instagram.

'No one is perfect, of course, but regarding the actions of some Al-Taawoun fans during the match against Al-Hilal: this isn't just about our club; it concerns our great religion, Islam.

'No matter how intense the rivalry or the situation, we should never stoop to gloating over the dead, engaging in slander, or attacking people's families or the deceased.

'We live in an Islamic country, and it is our duty to show the world what Islam truly represents—a religion of love, tolerance, and respect. I hope we can leverage the massive attention our league is receiving to project the best possible image of Islam.

'By doing so, we might foster goodwill and help others learn about our faith. That is the message I wanted to convey; I felt a personal obligation, as a Muslim living in this great Islamic nation, to speak out against what is happening—because it is wrong and unacceptable.'

Sports.title: Why Tottenham can't score a goal after £320m spending spree: Lost Mathys Tel is thinking like a playmaker, gambling on versatile wide men has backfired - and how Omar Marmoush looks the best fit to end barren start
Sports.content:
Why Tottenham can't score a goal after £320m spending spree: Lost Mathys Tel is thinking like a playmaker, gambling on versatile wide men has backfired - and how Omar Marmoush looks the best fit to end barren start

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Almost an hour had passed after the final whistle on Saturday when Tottenham’s manager Roberto De Zerbi arrived to do his press conference. There is a temptation to think his side could have spent that time on the pitch and still wouldn’t have scored against a team of mannequins.

He would go on to tell us about ‘blockages’, which might have applied to the Everton backline in a 0-0 draw, but in this instance involved something else – it was a discussion about the mental hurdles his forward players are facing in front of goal.

In short, he said they lack confidence. Overthinking has crept in. The weight of recent history is pressing them down and, like a golfer with the yips, they find themselves unable to pull the trigger.

The wait for a Tottenham goal in the league now measures in excess of six hours, dating back to the 43rd minute of the final game of last season against Everton. Palhinha could be the answer to a quiz question at this point. That they have drawn blanks in all four Premier League fixtures this season is a club record and sits horrendously against the backdrop of summer spending to the tune of around £320million.

One bookmaker’s social media account had a little play with those figures of £320million and six hours and came up with a decent gag: ‘You could make and watch Titanic twice for that.’

De Zerbi and Spurs fans won’t necessarily appreciate their role in yet another punchline.

Roberto De Zerbi suggested his Tottenham side had mental hurdles to overcome after a fourth match without scoring

What are his options?

Therein lies the problem – De Zerbi doesn’t have many, or possibly any of top-half calibre, if that remains an aspiration.

During a record-breaking transfer window, Spurs brought in three wingers, a left back, three centre-backs, two midfielders and a back-up goalkeeper. With Richarlison tucked away in exile, that left Dominic Solanke as the only fully-designated senior striker.

Solanke, for some context, hasn’t scored in the league since March and was utterly anonymous on Saturday – 19 touches, no shots.

Tottenham’s recruitment has instead gambled on the versatility of men better suited to wide positions. One of those is Omar Marmoush, who started on left wing against Everton having played up front against Nottingham Forest, and the other is Mathys Tel. He replaced Solanke after an hour and clearly irritated De Zerbi by turning backwards too often rather than towards goal.

Dominic Solanke has not scored in the league since March and was anonymous on Saturday

Is Marmoush the solution longer term?

That feels like the best fit for the way De Zerbi wants to play, which is currently wedded to positional fluidity and fewer fixed points in the team. The notion is that his striker can wander to deeper spots, sucking in the marker and then attacking the space with a wide man or No10.

Those interchanges were a feature of Saturday’s game all over the pitch – Archie Gray and Savio occasionally swapped spots when Gray overlapped on the right, Andy Robertson and Marmoush would do likewise on the left, and Marmoush would often change with Solanke. At its best, it can work and its worst, it is a watery mess – at the weekend and against Nottingham Forest, it was the latter.

But Marmoush’s mobility lends itself to this brief. We saw in Germany that he can finish and his chances to replicate the numbers at Manchester City were stymied by the presence of Erling Haaland. Solanke has suffered injuries for the past 18 months, but he has not looked close to the reliable finisher he was at Bournemouth in the 2023-24 campaign.

More pertinently, Solanke also looks less comfortable than Marmoush when he is asked to drop into deeper positions to satisfy De Zerbi’s grand vision. With so many other left wingers in the squad, including Savio, who played off the right on Saturday, there would be no direct consequence to moving Marmoush forward.

Omar Marmoush looks better suited to De Zerbi's plans and can operate in deeper positions

The deeper problem…

Call it the Tottenham paradox. They have an assortment of attacking options but are creating very little – the issue runs deeper than finishing, because you can only finish what you create. In the past two games, Tottenham have had one meaningful shot on target, and that came close to the end against Everton when Jordan Pickford had to save from Lucas Bergvall.

Savio can terrify defences with his acceleration, which he showed early against Vitalii Mykolenko, whom he skinned twice. But his deliveries and decision making with the final ball were poor and far below the expectation of a £75m signing. When Mykolenko found his bearings in that duel, Savio found no way to adapt and lost himself down blind alleys. He became irrelevant to the match.

Mateus Fernandes cost £10m more than Savio and has been slow to suggest it was well spent.

He is aggressively minded and can be fun to watch at full speed, but his four touches to control a ball when clean through in the first half was a calamitous waste of a good chance. It wasn’t isolated – he needs to be decisive, especially as the most expensive recruit of the bunch, Sandro Tonali, is drifting through games. Does Tonali even want to be there?

The Tel episode was interesting, because De Zerbi was right to question his striking instincts. The coach believes he can play up front, on the thin basis that he has played there before (albeit with two goals from his 15 games as a striker last season), but Tel is still thinking like a playmaker.

One problem related to Tel is that too many of Tottenham’s attackers do not see it as their responsibility to score the goals. Maybe that is an upshot of De Zerbi’s fluidity vision. But where is the wisdom in publicly berating a 21-year-old, as De Zerbi did on the pitch after the game?

Savio can terrify defences with his acceleration but faded after an impressive start against Everton

Mateus Fernandes taking four touches to control the ball when clean through was a calamitous waste of a good chance

De Zerbi was right to question Mathys Tel's striking instincts, but there was a lack of wisdom shown by doing it publicly

Delusion or deficiency?

De Zerbi spoke passionately after the game and, predictably, believes it will all be okay in the long run. Having kept Tottenham up, he deserves some benefit of the doubt but their start to this campaign inspires little confidence. The small pockets of booing from the crowd at the whistle would suggest a crisis is not far away.

However, De Zerbi was right to highlight the first 30 minutes of the match, when his side were quick on the ball and occasionally dominant. His argument is that if they could sustain that level beyond an hour, they probably win the game. Maybe, but it’s moot – they couldn’t and didn’t.

It was also a thin excuse when he argued that he has had less than a fortnight with the group and legs are tired after the World Cup – these are conditions under which all teams are operating and only Fulham, Aston Villa and Coventry sit beneath Spurs. After they face Liverpool in the League Cup on Tuesday, Tottenham play Villa in the league on Saturday – if they lose there will be an escalating feeling of crisis and even fewer excuses.

Sports.title: Furious Mikel Arteta is beginning to sound a lot like Sir Alex Ferguson after his latest referee outburst - but this is why it could backfire for Arsenal
Sports.content:
Three points secured on a gritty night away in Sunderland. After what happened here last time out for Arsenal in November, Brian Brobbey’s injury-time equaliser halting a five-game winning run, many assumed Mikel Arteta would be chuffed afterwards. It’s now five wins in a row and, just as crucially, a show of defiance in many ways. Bruno Guimaraes’ stunning strike – including a cupped ear celebration to a club who detest him from his Newcastle days – and David Raya’s world-class save to deny Enzo Le Fee’s spot-kick both typified this. Yet, Arteta strode into the post-match press conference with steam coming from his ears. I opened proceedings, asking about John Brooks’ controversial decision to award the Black Cats a penalty on 54 minutes. Ezri Konsa, who had a tough night at the hands of many wrestling jousts with Brobbey, was embroiled in another such battle – this time with Dan Ballard. Mikel Arteta was incensed despite Arsenal earning a hard fought 2-0 victory over Sunderland Arteta claimed the decision to award Sunderland a penalty was 'not acceptable' and compared Dan Ballard's action to a 'judo roll' David Raya saved the resulting penalty but Arteta hit out at the awarding of the spot-kick post match Both had hold of each other’s shirts in the area as the ball arrived, Ballard falling to the deck. Brooks’ call for a penalty was very soft, incorrect even, the pair each culpable for the holding. Le Fee stepped up to take the resulting penalty, which Raya sprang at full stretch to tip onto the right-hand post. The memory of that save went out of the window initially for Arteta, though, incensed over the decision. ‘(What) we have to go through today in my opinion is not acceptable,’ Arteta fumed. ‘I watched it 20 times, and I cannot find a way to understand how we even think to give a penalty. 'But I'm sad that we have to discuss in such a beautiful game something at this level that has the gravity to change the course of the season, and it can cost you the championship. 'It's a judo roll.’ It was Newcastle away all over again, that night in November 2023 springing to mind. On that occasion, Mikel Arteta described the decision to award Anthony Gordon’s winning goal against Arsenal as ‘disgraceful’ and ‘embarrassing’. Arteta wants to make sure that the refereeing fraternity are aware that any major decisions which, in his eyes, go incorrectly against Arsenal will be called out His comments post-match sounded a lot like legendary Man United boss Sir Alex Ferguson While Arteta was right to be aggrieved over the decision, but needs to be careful as such forthrightness could go against Arsenal if he is seen to be putting undue pressure on referees Again, walking into the room, the Spaniard was full of anger and you had a sense of the tirade he was about to unfurl. Rewinding back to Arsenal’s last-gasp escape against West Ham at the end of last season, where the VAR overturned Callum Wilson’s equaliser, Arteta had said he now ‘realised how difficult and how big the referee’s job is’. He had forgotten about this when it came to Brooks’ judgement. There was an element of Sir Alex Ferguson about his words. Winning wasn’t enough. He wants to make sure that the refereeing fraternity are aware that any major decisions which, in his eyes, go incorrectly against Arsenal will be called out. A further line channelled his inner Ferguson. ‘I cannot find an explanation, honestly. That's why I'm going to try to find an explanation now,’ he said. The Spaniard was right to be aggrieved over the decision, but needs to be careful. Such forthrightness could go against Arsenal if he is deemed to be putting undue pressure on referees. On the other side, it also showed the wider mindset at Arsenal. Having tasted a first league title in 22 years, and experiencing such a tight finish last time round, Arteta and Arsenal are not leaving anything to chance. They know how tight the margins are and want to get ahead of the curve. Making a point about refereeing decisions now is a psychological marker. That can have an effect in the months to come when a tight, game-changing call arises. Every point counts at this level. On this decision, Arteta was right, Brooks’s call harsh because of the level of contact Ballard and Konsa had placed on each other. Arsenal, though, do like to get physical in the area so need to be careful themselves going forward. It remains to be seen what level of restraint Arteta can keep going forward, for he’s on a tightrope.

Sports.title: Shocking moment Shane Lowry is caught on hot mic saying spectators 'deserve to get hit' after errant tee shot at the Irish Open
Sports.content:
Shane Lowry has come under fire after being heard saying a group of spectators 'deserve to get hit' after an errant tee shot in their direction at the Irish Open.

Lowry, who leads his home tournament heading into Sunday's final round, struck the errant tee shot on the 18th on Saturday.

The 39-year-old Irishman pulled his tee shot way to the left on the course, inadvertently sending it in the direction of spectators stood behind the ropes in a viewing area.

Lowry could be heard urgently shouting 'fore, fore' in a bid to warn the spectators that the ball was heading in their direction.

Footage showed the spectators, who were near a group of marshals, remaining stationary despite his warning.

Lowry was then caught by microphones stating: 'They deserve to get hit.'

Shane Lowry will want this one back, for a few different reasonspic.twitter.com/H39UYnNUHJ — Balls.ie (@ballsdotie) September 12, 2026

Shane Lowry came under fire from fans after appearing to suggest a group of supporters 'deserve to get hit' at the Irish Open

Several fans hit out at Lowry for the remark on social media, calling for the Irishman to apologise to the fans.

'He would never have said that when he was starting his career off? Paying punters cheering him on. How dare he. The fans deserve an apology. Who does he think he is?' one fan wrote.

'He should apologise or be fined. Horrible comment to make,' another said.

'An absolute disgrace, some role model,' a third said, while another wrote 'Your man wishing spectators and or volunteers deserved to be hit by a snap hook with a driver! Can do some serious damage.'

Some other fans were more sympathetic towards Lowry's outburst, suggesting that his comment was made in apparent frustration at the fans failing to move after his warning.

Despite the tee shot, Lowry was able to save par on the 18th to take a four-shot lead into the final round, as he looks to secure his first victory since 2022.

Lowry, who set a course-record 62 on Friday at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg, thanked the crowd for their support following his round.

'I feel like I did a great job today of staying in the moment and playing my own game,' Lowry said.

Lowry appeared to make the comment in frustration after fans failed to heed his warning to move clear of his errant tee shot

'I had so much fun out there on the back nine, the crowds were incredible and cheered me on the whole way home.

'Hopefully they do the same tomorrow.'

Lowry had kept his focus on a day when US President Donald Trump's arrival, which came as part of a two-day visit to Ireland, had briefly led to a halt in play.

The Irish star, whose closest challenger is Jacob Skov Olesen, will be hoping to seal victory at the tournament for the first time since 2009.

Sports.title: Chris Kamara's son breaks down in tears as Sky Sports icon opens up on health battle
Sports.content:
Chris Kamara's son breaks down in tears as Sky Sports icon opens up on health battle

Sky Sports icon Chris Kamara discussed his health battle on the BBC after taking part in the Great North Run

View 2 Images Chris Kamara spoke about his health during the Great North Run (Image: BBC)

Chris Kamara's son Jack became emotional after the popular TV presenter discussed his health battle during the Great North Run. The 68-year-old was interviewed by BBC One after running alongside his son and broadcast partner Ben Shephard on Sunday.

‌



The former Sky Sports pundit revealed his speech apraxia diagnosis in 2022, later deciding to step away from his presenting work. The neurological disorder affects the brain's ability to plan and coordinate movements needed to speak clearly.

‌



Kamara is an ex-professional footballer whose playing career saw him star for various clubs, but it was through his work on Sky Sports that he became a household name. His presenting jobs included hosting Goals on Sunday alongside Shephard for more than two decades.

‌



After finishing the race, Chris shared his amazement at having got through it. The TV host's reaction brought an emotional response from his son Jack, who was moved to tears, while Shephard championed his friend's effort.

Andy Burnham joins tens of thousands to take part in biggest ever Great North Run READ MORE :

"When I got to the line I really couldn't believe it and then my legs couldn't believe it either and then they collapsed below me," Chris Kamara said. "It was so emotional getting around that track. I'm back, I know I'm not really back but I am back yeah."

Responding to Kamara's feat, his son Jack fought back tears as he said: "I'm so proud. He's come a long way. He could barely walk a few years ago so to do that is just unbelievable. I know he says it all the time but it's just crazy."

‌



"You cannot underestimate what an extraordinary challenge Kammy set himself by agreeing to do this," Ben Shephard said. "It was a privilege for me to run alongside one of my best mates."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

He continued: "Because every step of the way we had to be careful of Kammy's balance. So it was, the concentration of everybody. But he just didn't stop. He was relentless. And like he said, the emotion crossing the line was off the charts. Running along here, the noise from the crowd was sensational.

‌



"For me it's a privilege to watch you battle but to see how the family have supported Kammy every step of the way and it's not been easy and that was something I will cherish for the rest of my life sharing that with you."

View 2 Images Chris Kamara's son Jack had an emotional reaction to his dad's words (Image: BBC )

Kamara has spoken openly about his journey with speech apraxia and recently gave an update during an appearance on ITV's This Morning last month, which Shephard was hosting alongside Cat Deeley.

‌



He said: "I'm feeling great, my voice has quickened up and I'm so much better. [Shephard] kept onto me, my carer there, he's been amazing. He's been there for me the whole time, he looks after me so much, but having someone behind you keep saying, 'You're still the same person as you were before', is amazing."

The trio were raising money for Prostate Cancer UK, a cause Chris described as "so important". He also called on viewers to get themselves tested, even if they are symptomless.

"Absolutely. Please do it. Even if you've got no symptoms whatsoever, prostate cancer might creep up on you but if you go to a doctor and you'll be fine."

Article continues below

Chris, Ben and Jack are running for Prostate Cancer UK at the AJ Bell Great North Run, raising funds for better treatments and tests for men, and helping to move one step closer to a national screening programme for all men and saving thousands of lives.

Sports.title: Furious Man Utd fans plan derby protest against owners over 'disgraceful' treatment
Sports.content:
Furious Man Utd fans plan derby protest against owners over 'disgraceful' treatment

Manchester United will take on Manchester City in the first instalment of the Manchester derby on Sunday but Old Trafford could look very different to normal during the game

View 2 Images Man Utd fans are set to protest against Manchester City (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United fans are set to abandon their Stretford End flags in protest at a controversial ticketing ban. The Red Devils have suspended hundreds of season ticket holders.

‌



Those suspected of touting have been hit with bans, with 685 tickets in all having been affected, albeit some of those maintain their innocence.

‌



The probe hasn’t been well received by supporters, with many now choosing to take action ahead of Sunday’s Manchester derby at Old Trafford. Fan group The Red Army have revealed that they will not unfurl their regular banners against Manchester City and will instead hold one above the player’s tunnel that will read: “The way you treat us is a disgrace.”

‌



A statement from the fan group read: “This isn’t a ‘TRA’ message, it’s a message on behalf of every genuine fan group, match-going supporter, supporters’ club and fan representative who has either contacted us directly or been negatively impacted by the recent behaviour of the club.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



“It’s an honest, heartfelt cry for recognition from the maligned, vilified, and misrepresented beating heart of our football club – the generational match-going supporters.

“Neither is this solely a ‘ Manchester United ’ problem, this is a league-wide crisis that should be addressed at every club, regardless of rivalries and history. Without drastic changes, there will be no rivalries in the future vision for football shared by the decision makers.”

Away from The Red Army, another fan group, The 1958, are set to hold a post-game march in protest.

‌



United have already spoken out on their system and ensured that anyone affected was only suspected of making a profit from selling the tickets on. A club statement read: "Bans were issued where there was significant misuse of the ticketing system for financial gain.

View 2 Images Man Utd fans will not sure their usual banners in the Stretford End (Image: Getty Images)

"This included the operation of organised ticketing networks, which were controlling, selling and distributing tickets from hundreds of accounts.

‌



"These actions undermine fair access to tickets for genuine supporters and have no place at Manchester United.

"Our focus now turns to ensuring these tickets are returned to our supporters. All season tickets released through this process will be offered to supporters on the season ticket waiting list."

Sunday’s protest will just be the latest in a long line of demonstrations targeted at United’s club ownership. The much-maligned Glazer family have regularly been the target of protests, while Sir Jim Ratcliffe has also felt the wrath of a number of United fans for the decisions he has made at Old Trafford since arriving at the club.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo demands action after Ruben Neves targeted by sick Diogo Jota chants
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo demands action after Ruben Neves targeted by sick Diogo Jota chants

Former Wolverhampton Wanderers star Ruben Neves was the target of horrendous chants about Diogo Jota during his most recent outing for Saudi side Al-Hilal

View 2 Images Neves was the target of some horrendous chants (Image: Getty Images)

Cristiano Ronaldo has called for any fans who mocked the death of Diogo Jota in front of Ruben Neves to never be allowed in a stadium again. Neves, who has been plying his trade in Saudi Arabia since 2023, was in action for Al-Hilal against Al-Taawoun on Saturday.

‌



His side ran out 6-0 victors on the day - ex-Arsenal star Gabriel Martinelli netting a hat-trick, while England’s Ollie Watkins scored twice. But the win was overshadowed by some vile chants from supporters.

‌



Video footage has shown Neves reacting to supporters seemingly mockingly singing the name of former Liverpool and Wolves forward Jota, who died in a devastating car crash alongside his brother Andre Silva in July 2025.

‌



Speaking to reporters after the game, Neves said: “I hope they don't go to prayer later.” Ronaldo has now given his take and called for serious action for those found responsible.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Taking to Instagram, he wrote: "The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour. This is no longer football, and there have to be limits. People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again."

Neves was close friends with Jota, the pair having played together both at Wolves and with the Portuguese national team. The midfielder has previously revealed that he still talks to his friend in a group chat, while he also has a tattoo of his former teammate on his leg.

"I still talk to him. Few people know this. We have a WhatsApp group with Rute (Jota's widow) and Diogo, and it's still there, and we continue to talk there.

‌



“Whenever something special happens, I have the conversations archived on my WhatsApp so I can continue to send him messages."

Saudi Arabian international Saleh Abu Al-Shamat was also one of those to speak out in the aftermath of Saturday’s incident. Taking to Instagram, he wrote: “I wanted to draw attention to something we all witnessed today. I felt it was my duty - as a Muslim - to share this and raise awareness.

View 2 Images Neves was good friends with Diogo Jota after playing together at Wolves (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“No one is perfect, of course, but regarding the actions of some Al-Taawoun fans during the match against Al-Hilal: this isn't just about our club; it concerns our great religion, Islam.

“No matter how intense the rivalry or the situation, we should never stoop to gloating over the dead, engaging in slander, or attacking people's families or the deceased.

“We live in an Islamic country, and it is our duty to show the world what Islam truly represents—a religion of love, tolerance, and respect. I hope we can leverage the massive attention our league is receiving to project the best possible image of Islam.

Article continues below

“By doing so, we might foster goodwill and help others learn about our faith. That is the message I wanted to convey; I felt a personal obligation, as a Muslim living in this great Islamic nation, to speak out against what is happening—because it is wrong and unacceptable.”

Sports.title: Jordan McCann reveals huge purse for Big Stacks fight - 'I can't box for s***'
Sports.content:
Jordan McCann reveals huge purse for Big Stacks fight - 'I can't box for s***'

Rapper Jordan McCann was stopped by Big Stacks in the second round of their grudge match when he was unable to see out of one eye

View Image Big Stacks beat Jordan McCann

Jordan McCann has revealed he was paid £150,000 to have his face bashed up by Big Stacks.

‌



The rapper returned to the ring on Saturday night for his second fight under the Misfits Boxing banner. But he left it three minutes later with one eye swollen shut as Big Stacks dominated from the opening bell before the fight was stopped on the ringside doctor's orders.

‌



McCann had previously taken on Ibiza Final Boss in June when the fight went the four-round distance and the pair could clash again in Manchester in December. But after his second defeat in three months, McCann said: "Big up Misfits; it's not just about the money, but I did get £150,000, which can help my family," he said. "But I can't fight for s***. I'm not a boxer. This is what happens; you sell yourself, but you can't play boxing. Look at my face.

‌



UK's Hardest Man Big Stacks leaves Jordan McCann with eye swollen shut READ MORE :

"Stacks is still a sausage, but respect to him. He did his job and respect to his coach and his team, and apologies to my team. It is what it is. I should take these camps seriously, but I don't. I blag it for Instagram, but this is what happens when you play boxing. I got away with it the first time, but these 10-ounce gloves ain't a game."

Big Stacks - whose real name is Charlie Robert and who calls himself the UK's hardest man - said after the fight: "I was too powerful, I kept catching him. It was harder than I thought it would be. I thought it would be easier so I will have to train harder for tougher opponents. I lost my skill and got into a scrap, but it was always going to be a scrap with Jordan. But I jabbed his head off and hurt him. My cardio was s*** again but I'll get better."

Article continues below

Asked who he wanted to fight next, he called out Martyn Ford, who is also known as the World's Strongest Man. "I'm the hardest man and I'm here to stay," he added. "Martyn Ford, he's a big donut; I want him next. He's big but he's a prick. I want to smash his head. I want to kick his head in."

Sports.title: Big Stacks vs Jordan McCann Misfits LIVE results including Ibiza Final Boss
Sports.content:
Big Stacks stopped Jordan McCann after leaving his rival's eye swollen shut.

Big Stacks immediately made his size pay as he repeatedly landed his jab on McCann. The rapper was struggling to see out of his right eye and when the fight was paused in the second round for it to be inspected, the doctor had no option but to wave off the contest, handing Big Stacks victory. He then said: "I was too powerful, I kept catching him.

"It was harder than I thought it would be. I thought it would be easier so I will have to train harder for tougher opponents. I lost my skill and got into a scrap, but it was always going to be a scrap with Jordan. But I jabbed his head off and hurt him. My cardio was s*** again but I'll get better."

Sports.title: Chris Eubank Jr ruthlessly trolls Conor Benn in 11 words after Ryan Garcia fight disaster
Sports.content:
Chris Eubank Jr ruthlessly trolls Conor Benn in 11 words after Ryan Garcia fight disaster

After Conor Benn endured a difficult evening in Las Vegas against Ryan Garcia, Chris Eubank Jr could not resist reigniting his feud with his former rival

View 3 Images Chris Eubank Jr was in attendance to watch Ryan Garcia overcome Conor Benn (Image: Fight Hub TV)

Chris Eubank Jr could not resist having a dig at Conor Benn after his former rival was stopped by Ryan Garcia. Benn, 29, did not even get through two rounds before Garcia was crowned the winner.

‌



The American retained his WBC welterweight title by flooring the Brit with a ferocious right hand. The Essex based fighter managed to climb up from the canvas after the count of eight, but the fight was ended by referee Tom Taylor when Garcia unleashed on the Brit while he was pinned on the ropes.

‌



It was Benn's first bout at welterweight in four years and he made the weight after an agonising weight cut which often left him in tears. There was little sympathy from Eubank Jr, who was beaten by Benn in their second bout after he had to boil his own weight down to reach 160lbs last year.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

After Garcia's hand was raised in triumph, Eubank Jr took to social media and said: "Welcome to the ’fighting after cutting too much weight’ club… Enjoy.”

Before their second fight, Eubank Jr went through his own agony in a bit to get down to the 160lb weight. Despite his efforts, he missed it by 0.05lb and had to pay a penalty of £375,000 to Benn as a result.

‌



Before Benn took on Garcia in Sin City, he opened up about the pain he went through to get back down to welterweight. He said to talkSPORT: "I've been dragged down to the pits of hell, had a fight with Satan, and come back to life.

View 3 Images Garcia outclassed Conor Benn (Image: AP Photo/Ian Maule)

"When I mean hard, I mean hard. That's why I'm going straight to 160[lbs] after this. This is the fight. This is the real fight. I have been dying for 15 weeks... I'm on almost a 1000 calorie deficit a day.

‌



"When I talk about the emotional breakdowns I've had in camp. I've been sobbing, crying, can't even get up the stairs. To that degree. To now get here and feel unbelievable. But I had to do those hard yards; I'd rather it be hard then, and easy now."

Before the bout, Garcia, perhaps sensing vulnerability, promised to end the fight within five rounds. In the end, he only needed two to retain his crown.

View 3 Images Benn made a standing eight count but the fight was stopped soon after (Image: Zuffa Boxing via Getty Images)

‌



Afte his win, Garcia said: "I've always had a right hand but it's always been injured. I was so prepared and so focused, and what a performance. I knew he was going to put me under pressure in the first round so I let him have his way a little bit.

"Then in the next round I stood my ground a little bit. He was coming in reckless and you can't do that with me; he would have been better running around for the first three rounds. I've got thunder in both hands and they're ready to go. I'm here, I'm the champion and I'm not going to f*** around."

After losing Benn took to social media and wrote: "Not my night, no excuses. Ryan Garcia, you’re a great champion."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
