Nigerians have again lost money to a collapsed online investment scheme, PXES, which stopped paying investors in early September 2026 and then became inaccessible. The platform had promised returns of 25% to 50%, with some packages as high as 120%, according to reports.

What the PXES platform promised and how it fell apart

PXES marketed itself as a high-yield online investment platform, drawing in savers with the promise of unusually large returns in a short period. Victims report losses ranging from tens of thousands to millions of naira, with many saying they invested money meant for rent, school fees or small businesses.

When payments stopped in early September 2026, the platform became inaccessible, leaving investors unable to withdraw funds or contact operators. Angry investors stormed PXES offices in parts of Adamawa and Kogi states, a sign of how quickly frustration turned to confrontation.

The collapse follows a familiar script in Nigeria’s crowded market for quick-return schemes. Platforms often begin by paying early investors, building trust and word-of-mouth momentum, before freezing withdrawals once new money slows.

Nigeria’s long history of Ponzi losses

The PXES collapse is not an isolated event. The Securities and Exchange Commission said in 2025 that Nigerians had lost over ₦316 billion to Ponzi schemes and unlicensed fund managers, a figure that underscores the scale of the problem.

The Guardian cited an even larger estimate of ₦1.7 trillion lost over nine years since 2016. That period includes some of the most notorious cases in the country’s financial history.

MMM Nigeria, which launched in 2015, froze transactions in December 2016 after attracting about three million Nigerians with a promised 30% monthly return. The scheme’s collapse left a generation of savers wary of formal finance and hungry for alternatives.

The money and power stakes behind the scams

Recent collapses show how large the market for quick-return scams has become. CBEX was reported to have taken about ₦1.3 trillion from investors, and the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission later said it had recovered some funds and arrested promoters.

The political economy backdrop is weak trust in formal finance, high inflation and unemployment pressure. Many Nigerians see high-yield schemes as a rational response to an economy where traditional savings accounts offer negative real returns.

Regulators are racing to keep up with fast-moving digital platforms that can launch, attract funds and disappear within weeks. The challenge is that enforcement often comes after the damage is done, leaving victims with little recourse.

Who gains and who loses in the PXES collapse

The clearest losers are the individual savers who put money into PXES, many of whom are unlikely to recover their funds. The promoters, if identified and prosecuted, could face charges, but recovery rates in such cases are historically low.

Formal financial institutions also lose, as each collapse deepens public distrust of any investment product. That distrust pushes more Nigerians toward informal schemes, creating a cycle that is hard to break.

Regulators face pressure to show they can protect ordinary savers. The Securities and Exchange Commission has warned repeatedly about unlicensed investment schemes, but warnings alone have not stopped the flow of money into them.

The regional read-through for West Africa

Nigeria’s Ponzi problem is a warning for other West African markets where digital finance is growing faster than regulatory capacity. The same conditions that make Nigeria fertile ground for scams exist in neighbouring countries: high inflation, weak formal savings options and widespread mobile phone use.

For investors and professionals watching the region, the pattern matters. Each high-profile collapse erodes confidence in digital finance, making it harder for legitimate fintech companies to build trust.

The South-South angle is also relevant. As African economies deepen ties with Brazil, India and other emerging powers, the flow of capital and financial innovation brings both opportunity and risk. The challenge is building regulatory frameworks that can keep pace without stifling innovation.

What to watch next after the PXES platform, which analysts and local outlets describe as a suspected Ponzi scheme,

The immediate question is whether authorities will identify and arrest the promoters behind PXES. The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission has acted in past cases, including CBEX, but the speed and effectiveness of enforcement vary.

Longer term, the test is whether Nigeria can shift savers toward regulated investment products that offer competitive returns. That requires rebuilding trust in formal finance, a task that will take years, not months.

For now, the PXES collapse is another reminder that promises of 25% to 50% returns, let alone 120%, are almost always too good to be true. The pattern is well documented, but the human cost keeps rising.

Frequently Asked Questions

What was the PXES platform? PXES was an online investment platform that promised returns of 25% to 50%, with some packages as high as 120%, before stopping payments in early September 2026 and becoming inaccessible. How much have Nigerians lost to Ponzi schemes? The Securities and Exchange Commission said in 2025 that Nigerians had lost over ₦316 billion to Ponzi schemes and unlicensed fund managers, while The Guardian cited an estimated ₦1.7 trillion lost over nine years since 2016. What should investors do to avoid Ponzi schemes in Nigeria? Investors should be wary of any platform promising returns of 25% or more, verify that investment firms are licensed by the Securities and Exchange Commission, and avoid putting money into schemes that are not transparent about how returns are generated.

World.title: Kenya and Its Neighbours Are Reaching for Treason Charges Against Their Critics
World.content:
Kenya · POLITICS

Key Facts — What happened Kenyan authorities have repeatedly used treason rhetoric and treason charges against activists and opposition figures since the June 2024 anti-tax protests.

— The catch Treason is among the most serious offences in Kenya’s Penal Code and can attract the death penalty, making it a powerful political weapon even when cases do not reach trial.

— Who it hits Activist Boniface Mwangi was arrested on 19 July 2025, and activist Bob Njagi was arrested on 24 June 2026 and the treason charge against him was dismissed for lack of evidence on 2 July 2026, over alleged incitement linked to the 25 June anniversary protests.

— The precedent In February 2018, opposition lawyer Miguna Miguna was charged with treason over the late Raila Odinga symbolic swearing-in, showing the charge has long been used against opposition symbolism.

— The regional pattern Uganda’s Kizza Besigye was abducted in Nairobi in November 2024 and later faced treason charges in Uganda, while Tanzania prosecuted Tundu Lissu for treason.

Kenya treason charges have become a recurring tool for framing political dissent as an existential threat, from the June 2024 parliament storming to arrests of activists in 2025 and 2026. The pattern extends across East Africa, where opposition figures face similar securitisation.

Kenya and its neighbours reach for treason charges against their critics

Kenya’s state has repeatedly used treason rhetoric and treason charges to frame dissent as an existential threat, especially around the June 2024 anti-tax protests and the later “Gen Z” mobilisations. Interior officials said investigators were examining alleged efforts to “overthrow” the government after protesters stormed parliament on 25 June 2024, while rights groups said the response was a crackdown on legitimate political expression.

How Kenya treason charges became a political weapon

The legal backdrop makes the charge especially potent. Kenya’s treason offence is among the most serious in the Penal Code and can attract the death penalty, making it a powerful political weapon even when cases do not reach trial.

Reuters documented an earlier precedent in February 2018, when opposition lawyer Miguna Miguna was charged over the late Raila Odinga symbolic swearing-in. That case underscored how treason has been used against opposition symbolism as well as violence.

The pattern intensified after the June 2024 protests. Interior officials framed the parliament storming as an attempted overthrow, while rights groups countered that the response was a crackdown on legitimate political expression.

The cases of Boniface Mwangi and Bob Njagi

A key recent case involved activist Boniface Mwangi. On 19 July 2025 police arrested him at his Lukenya home, and prosecutors initially pursued terrorism and money-laundering allegations.

Those counts were later dropped and substituted with a lesser firearms charge. The shift showed how serious initial charges can be used to detain and stigmatise before being quietly downgraded.

The following year, courts dismissed treason charges against activist Bob Njagi. He had been arrested on 24 June 2026 over alleged incitement linked to the 25 June anniversary protests.

A regional pattern of securitising opposition politics

The wider regional power context is similar. In Uganda, veteran opposition figure Kizza Besigye was abducted in Nairobi in November 2024 and later faced treason charges in Uganda.

Activists in 2026 accused Kenya of enabling that operation. The case, and Tanzania’s treason prosecution of Tundu Lissu, show a regional pattern of securitising opposition politics.

This pattern fits the broader contest over political space in Eastern Africa, where governments face pressure from younger, digitally mobilised populations. The Africa: The New Scramble pillar tracks how such internal dynamics intersect with external powers seeking influence in the region.

What the treason charges mean for investors and professionals

For investors and professionals operating in Kenya, the use of treason charges signals a political environment where dissent is treated as a security matter. That can affect perceptions of rule of law and political risk.

The June 2024 protests already disrupted business activity in Nairobi and other urban centres. A continuing pattern of securitising opposition could deter long-term investment that depends on predictable legal and political processes.

At the same time, the courts have shown some independence, as in the dismissal of charges against Bob Njagi. That mixed picture leaves businesses weighing immediate stability against longer-term governance concerns.

Who gains and who loses from the treason narrative

The government gains a rhetorical tool that casts critics as enemies of the state. That can rally supporters and justify expanded security powers.

Activists, opposition figures and civil society groups lose space for legitimate political expression. The threat of a death-penalty charge can chill protest even when cases are later dropped or dismissed.

Ordinary Kenyans also lose when dissent is suppressed, because accountability mechanisms weaken. The regional pattern suggests this is not an isolated tactic but part of a broader approach to managing opposition across Eastern Africa.

What to watch next in Kenya and the region

The anniversary protests on 25 June remain a flashpoint, and any new mobilisations could trigger fresh treason charges. Courts will be tested on whether they continue to dismiss weak cases or allow the charge to be used more aggressively.

Regionally, the Besigye case in Uganda and the Lissu case in Tanzania will show whether courts and regional bodies push back against securitised politics. Kenya’s role in the Besigye abduction remains a point of contention among activists.

For now, the pattern is clear: treason charges in Kenya are less about actual plots to overthrow the state and more about muzzling political dissent. The question is whether the courts and public pressure can reverse that trend.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the punishment for treason in Kenya? Treason is among the most serious offences in Kenya’s Penal Code and can attract the death penalty, making it a powerful political weapon even when cases do not reach trial. Who has faced treason charges in Kenya recently? Activist Bob Njagi was arrested on 24 June 2026 and the treason charge against him was dismissed for lack of evidence on 2 July 2026, over alleged incitement linked to the 25 June anniversary protests, but courts later dismissed the treason charges against him. Is the use of treason charges unique to Kenya? No, the pattern extends across East Africa, with Uganda charging Kizza Besigye and Tanzania prosecuting Tundu Lissu for treason in similar securitisation of opposition politics.

World.title: Belize to send another diplomatic note over Guatemalan presence in Sarstoon
World.content:
Belize to send another diplomatic note over Guatemalan presence in Sarstoon

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The Government of Belize will issue another diplomatic note to Guatemala following the latest confrontation in the Sarstoon River.

Foreign Minister Francis Fonseca says Belize must continue formally recording its objection whenever Guatemalan forces exercise what the Government considers illegal authority in the area.

Fonseca said the latest incident highlights the difficulties that will remain until the International Court of Justice issues its final ruling on the territorial dispute.

Despite those challenges, he said Belize continues to pursue a peaceful approach and remains engaged in dialogue with Guatemala.

Fonseca noted that there was a heavy presence of Guatemalan military boats, along with civilian vessels, during the latest incident.

He said the positive outcome was that no one was injured and the situation did not escalate into a more serious confrontation.

Belizean security forces were still able to hold a flag raising ceremony at the Forward Operating Base, with members of the Belize Territorial Volunteers participating.

Fonseca said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs will continue using both diplomatic protests and direct engagement with Guatemala.

He added that Prime Minister John Briceño also maintains communication with the Guatemalan government as part of efforts to avoid dangerous incidents.

Fonseca said the heavier Guatemalan military presence around the September celebrations period is not unusual because annual Belizean visits to the Sarstoon are publicly known.

World.title: OAS urges calm after Belizeans blocked from Sarstoon Island
World.content:
OAS urges calm after Belizeans blocked from Sarstoon Island

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The head of the Organization of American States is urging Belize and Guatemala to keep dialogue alive following the latest standoff at the Sarstoon River.

OAS Secretary General Albert Ramdin said he regretted Thursday’s incident, during which the Belize Territorial Volunteers were prevented from completing their annual trip around Sarstoon Island because of a significant Guatemalan presence in the area.

Reports indicate that Belizean participants were escorted by members of the Belize Defence Force and Coast Guard but could only travel as far as the Forward Operating Base after multiple Guatemalan military and civilian vessels were observed in the river.

Ramdin said the confrontation did not come as a complete surprise because the OAS had anticipated increased sensitivities surrounding Belize’s Independence celebrations.

He said both Belize and Guatemala have pledged to continue talking and that he has confidence in the foreign ministers of both countries to maintain communication.

Ramdin also noted that the OAS Adjacency Zone Office does not have a mandate covering all incidents involving rivers or other areas outside the western border zone.

Despite that limitation, he said the wider organization remains interested in peace and stability between the two countries while they await a final ruling from the International Court of Justice.

Ramdin said he hopes future incidents can be handled with clarity and restraint and stressed that neither government appears interested in escalation.

World.title: Halo BPO hiring work from home sales agents in Belize
World.content:
Halo BPO hiring work from home sales agents in Belize

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belizeans looking for a work from home opportunity can apply to join Halo BPO, which is currently recruiting qualified sales agents.

The company is offering a BZ$8.50 per hour position with a dialing schedule from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Belize time.

Halo BPO says it is particularly interested in applicants with experience in appointment setting or the home improvement industry.

Because the position is completely remote, applicants must have the equipment and internet connection necessary to work effectively from home.

Requirements include internet speeds of at least 40 Mbps for both downloads and uploads, a wired ethernet or LAN connection, a good quality USB headset, webcam and at least 8GB of RAM.

Applicants should also have a quad core processor of at least 2.0GHz and a quiet, distraction free workspace. SSD storage is preferred, while Chromebooks are not accepted.

Qualified Belizeans interested in applying can email [email protected] and should include their full name in the email subject line.

World.title: Jose Luis “Bones” Sosa killed in Orange Walk Town shooting
World.content:
Jose Luis “Bones” Sosa killed in Orange Walk Town shooting

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A man was shot and killed in Orange Walk Town sometime early Sunday morning.

The victim has been identified as Jose Luis Sosa, better known as “Bones.”

Initial reports of gunshots in the area began circulating shortly before 5:00 a.m., followed by information that a man had been shot.

Further information has since confirmed that Sosa died as a result of the shooting.

Police have not yet released full details surrounding the incident, including the exact location, possible motive or whether any suspects have been identified.

Sosa was known by many in Orange Walk by his nickname “Bones.”

Officials are expected to provide more information as the investigation continues.

Breaking Belize News extends condolences to Sosa’s family and loved ones.

This is a developing story and more details will be shared as they become available.

World.title: Sunshine dominates Belize today with only isolated showers expected
World.content:
Sunshine dominates Belize today with only isolated showers expected

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Mostly sunny skies and warm temperatures are expected across Belize today as generally fair weather continues.

The National Meteorological Service says Sunday will feature sunshine mixed with periods of cloudiness, while tonight will be partly cloudy.

Most communities should experience little rainfall, with showers or thunderstorms remaining isolated.

The main exception will be southern Belize, where a few more showers could develop during the morning hours.

Rainfall activity is then expected to decrease before another possibility of showers develops over the south tonight.

For the rest of Belize, conditions should remain largely dry and warm throughout the day and evening.

World.title: He was a ‘Traveller’, a ‘Bad Man’, a ‘Rude Boy’, a real ‘Land Shark’: Chinese liquor ‘durr’ busted on bicycle with schoolbag full of Revel and no liquor license
World.content:
He was a ‘Traveller’, a ‘Bad Man’, a ‘Rude Boy’, a real ‘Land Shark’: Chinese liquor ‘durr’ busted on bicycle with schoolbag full of Revel and no liquor license

By Breaking Belize News Staff: An Orange Walk businessman has been charged with keeping alcohol without a liquor licence after police allegedly found 16 small bottles of rum inside a school bag.

Police say two cops were on foot patrol on Baker Street at around 7:30 p.m. on September 9 when they saw Wu Peng Ling riding a bicycle carrying an empty Belikin crate and a brown school bag.

A search of the bag reportedly uncovered 16 small bottles of Gold Revel Rum along with a container holding money.

Police say Ling was unable to produce a liquor licence and was arrested.

According to the police report, officers had encountered Ling on two previous occasions in recent weeks — on September 2 with 22 small bottles of Revel Rum and on August 26 with another nine small bottles and money.

Ling was formally arrested and charged on September 10 with keeping alcohol without a licence. Police say he remained silent when cautioned.

World.title: Man allegedly stabbed by girlfriend at wedding reception with boxcutter over $20
World.content:
Man allegedly stabbed by girlfriend at wedding reception with boxcutter over $20

By Breaking Belize News Staff: An argument between a couple at a wedding reception near Ladyville allegedly ended with a man being cut on his hand with a box cutter.

Police received information at around 6:10 p.m. on September 10 of a stabbing at Hakim Shipyard near Mile 6.5 on the Philip Goldson Highway.

A 32-year-old man later told police that he had invited his girlfriend to the wedding, but an argument began after she became upset because he had not been answering her telephone calls.

According to the man, his girlfriend asked him to pay $20 to a relative who had transported her to the event. He initially refused but later agreed in an attempt to calm the situation.

The man alleged that as he handed over the money, his girlfriend reached into her purse, pulled out what appeared to be a black box cutter and swung it at him, cutting his right hand.

He reportedly ran into the establishment for assistance while his girlfriend left toward Ladyville.

The man was treated at the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital and requested court action. Police have listed the woman as wanted as the investigation continues.

World.title: Police investigating man who allegedly choked 10-year-old boy who hit his son with stick
World.content:
Police investigating man who allegedly choked 10-year-old boy who hit his son with stick

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating an allegation that an adult man choked a 10-year-old Belize City boy following an altercation between the child and another boy on Friday afternoon.

According to police, the 10-year-old reported that he and another boy were striking a cement verandah with separate pieces of stick when the other child struck him on the leg.

The boy said he retaliated by striking the other child below the eye.

Police say the other child’s father subsequently came outside and allegedly placed his hand around the 10-year-old’s neck and choked him.

The child visited the Precinct One Police Station with his mother and was issued a medico-legal form for his injuries.

Police have identified Abraham Baptist as a person they are seeking in connection with the investigation.

World.title: Surge in road deaths; at least 40 killed in crashes in last 28 days
World.content:
This file photo shows the motorcycle that collided with a Honda motorcar.

KINGSTON, Jamaica — At least 40 people were killed in motor vehicle crashes in the 28 days between August 14 and September 11, according to an analysis of the daily crash reports of the Island Traffic Authority (ITA).

According to the daily crash reports, 202 people were killed as a result of 174 fatal crashes as at August 14. Those figures included 49 motorcyclists. They also represented a 15 per cent decline or 36 fewer deaths when compared to the similar period in 2025. Fatal crashes were also down 16 per cent at that time.

Fast forward to Friday, September 11 and some of those gains have been eroded as is seen in the 242 deaths from 209 fatal crashes now being reported by the ITA. According to the ITA, fatalities have decreased by 10 per cent when compared to prior year while fatal crashes are down 10 per cent when compared with similar period in 2025. Overall, there are 26 fewer deaths when compared to the similar period in 2025.

As of September 11, motorcyclists account for 63 or 26 per cent of fatalities since the start of the year. Private motor vehicle drivers account for 55 or 23 per cent, while pedestrians account for 53 deaths or 22 per cent of all fatalities this year.

The ITA is also reporting that private motor vehicle passengers, account for 33 deaths or 14 per cent of fatalities, commercial motor vehicle passengers account for deaths 14 deaths or six per cent, and pillion passengers account for eight deaths or three per cent of fatalities since January 1.

Meanwhile, the group of road users determined to be the most vulnerable – pedestrians, pedalcyclists, motorcyclists and pillion passengers combined – account for 53 per cent of fatalities. Overall, passengers account for 24 per cent of all road deaths this year, while males and females account for 86 per cent and 15 per cent respectively of fatalities since the start of the year.

In the meantime, Westmoreland parish has recorded the highest number of fatalities, accounting for 13 per cent of fatalities since the start of 2026.

— Lynford Simpson

World.title: ‘Really, really sad’
World.content:
An undated picture of seven-year-old Keriecia Hutchinson and her four-year-old brother Samson Cameron, who died in a house fire in Smith Lane, Central Kingston, on Saturday.

GRIEF and anger were palpable in the Central Kingston community of Smith Lane on Saturday as it was confirmed that seven-year-old Keriecia Hutchinson and her four-year-old brother Samson Cameron had perished in a mid-morning house fire.

Residents remembered the two children who they said were promising and full of life while anger surged as people assigned blame for their deaths.

Keriecia was a grade one student at Calabar All-Age School, while Samson was a student of Calabar Basic School.

“The mother locked them up in the house and gone to a wholesale. She could have just left them out and asked any of wi to look on them,” charged one neighbour who, like her colleagues, refused to give their names.

“The mother do nothing wrong, the [son’s] father was here and him run go up there [to the room] before the fire get wicked and him run down back and say him can’t reach the children,” charged another neighbour.

Police on the scene refused to speak with the media to confirm or deny either claim, but the contention morphed into a physical battle between one woman — who was defending the children’s grandmother — and another female resident who was chastising the parents.

Police on the scene fired a number of shots in the air to separate the combatants and at least three people were later taken into custody.

But for most residents in Smith Lane the death of the two children was their main concern.

“Right yah now me feel really, really sad that the two kids lose them lives,” said one of the few residents willing to speak to the media on condition that she not be named.

“What I get to understand, the mother wasn’t here, she gone to the wholesale, but why did she lock the children inside? And when people call out and the father run inside, the door lock, and is like him forget the key so him panic. So when the door finally open and people a throw water — even me a throw out water — it did not save the children. It really, really sad,” said the woman.

She told the Jamaica Observer that Keriecia moved to live with her mother in Smith Lane when she was about two years old, while the son, “him a must be about four or five years old now, and him born right here so inna mi hand”, added the neighbour.

She said many residents tried to put the blaze out before the Jamaica Fire Brigade team arrived but they were unsuccessful.

Residents also had praise for a neighbour who they said soaked himself in water before entering the burning house after being told that the children were inside, but he was unable to rescue them.

“He is a hero, man. Him really try, but the children were not in the front room, they were in the back, and the little girl died hugging her brother trying to save him. You could see she was trying to help him,” said one man, who, like others, refused to give his name.

At press time Saturday the fire brigade had not determined the cause of the blaze, while there was no word on whether the people involved in the physical altercation had been charged.

An unofficial count by the Sunday Observer has shown four children have died in fires across the island since the start of this year.

World.title: ‘Why did my parents forsake me?’
World.content:
A 17-year-old boy is searching for answers, guidance, and assistance to turn his life around after a series of unfortunate events saw him moving in and out of five children’s homes without a solid plan for his future.

The recent high school graduate said he does not have a relationship with his parents, with both reportedly choosing not to play an active role in his life when he was just a few months old. He is being raised by his paternal grandmother who, he said, struggles to make ends meet and wants help to get him on the right track.

The young man shared that while in primary school he was bullied daily because he seemingly did not have any parents. He said he grew frustrated with the bullies and decided to fight back. During an altercation he said he accidentally damaged the car of a staff member of the institution.

He said attempts were made to contact his parents and grandmother, but they were unsuccessful. He ended up in State care.

“I went to five boys’ homes. I went to one in Clarendon, St Mary, Kingston, Spanish Town and Old Harbour [both in St Catherine]. The first three homes were nice, because I had friends there and people didn’t do anything to me, but the last home I didn’t like it because they started to molest me,” he told the Jamaica Observer.

“I was sleeping in my dorm and this boy molested me. They held me down in my sleep. It was five boys who did that to me…I was very scared,” he recounted, his voice filled with sadness.

He said the incident was reported to a staff member, who contacted his case worker. The young man said he was taken from that home and provided counselling. Another attempt was made to contact his grandmother, who eventually agreed to take him back in her care.

He said financial struggles were heightened when the house they were living in was destroyed by fire, leaving them with little to nothing to recover.

“I lost most of my clothes and things that I had. It was a rental house, so we had to find somewhere else to live,” recalled the 17-year-old.

He said they eventually found a new place to stay but lost a lot of things that they still need to replace, such as clothes and other household items.

Now out of high school, the 17-year-old said he is seeking assistance to turn his life around. However, his greatest wish is to have a relationship with his parents, especially his mother.

“Every day I get up I just feel sad, and I don’t know why. I don’t know why I didn’t get to meet my mother…When I get up and I see a parent with a son or daughter, I always say to myself, ‘Why did my parents forsake me?’ because I never do them anything. Whenever I see children with their mother, I just start to cry and just feel sadness. I cry every single day,” he told the Sunday Observer.

The 17-year-old said he is still in contact with a counsellor who encourages him that better days are ahead, but he is still left with more questions than answers about why his life had to be this way.

“I would be happy if I had a relationship with them. I just want a relationship with my mom. People always trouble me that I don’t have any mother,” he said.

Now a high school graduate, he is uncertain about where life will take him, and needs some guidance and assistance.

“I would love to get some help to get my driver’s licence and maybe some clothes, because I want to get a job and go to work. I also want to go to school. I was thinking of applying to HEART [Human Employment and Resource Training/National Service Training Agency Trust] and learn a skill, but I need some help.

“I need support, because I’m going to be 18 soon and I want to learn how to drive and stuff so that I can take care of myself. I just want support,” he said.

His grandmother said that, over the years, she has tried her best, but with ageing and a lack of resources there is only so much she can do.

“I get help from my sisters, but that is it. Otherwise, it’s just him and me alone,” she said.

She added that the situation is made worse by the fact that she is often left with questions she cannot answer.

“Almost every day him get up and ask me what happened with his parents, and if somebody did something to run them away. I don’t know the answer. His mother just left him with me, and his father is not around,” she said.

She, too, pleaded for assistance for her grandson, wanting him to have a better future than his past.

“I would love it if him can get some assistance to go to HEART and learn a skill. He needs clothes and other things, too,” she pleaded.

World.title: Greatness Weekend marked as economic booster for Kgn
World.content:
Patron Shavo’neil Edwards poses at the last staging of Greatness Pink & White Brunch.

EXECUTIVE director of the Tourism Enhancement Fund (TEF), Dr Carey Wallace has underscored the importance of collaboration as Jamaica’s entertainment sector in driving economic growth and advancing the country’s development.

Wallace made the call on Tuesday during the official launch of Greatness Weekend at the Jamaica Pegasus hotel in New Kingston, where tourism officials, event promoters, and other stakeholders gathered ahead of the four-day entertainment series slated for October 16-19.

“For Jamaica to get to where we want — to a First World, developed country — we need to have more collaborations like what we’re seeing here tonight,” Wallace told the gathering.

He said Jamaica already possesses many of the ingredients necessary to become a developed nation, pointing particularly to the strength of its people, culture, and international brand.

“Jamaica has all the ingredients to be an amazing, developed country. In fact, when the British had it, it was their most-prized colony. We are a people that are revered anywhere in the world we go. When you say you are Jamaican you see people’s pupils dilate; people get excited. So, let us deliver,” Wallace said.

He added that tourism has an important role to play in ensuring Jamaica’s resources and global appeal translate into tangible benefits for its people.

“We, in tourism, recognise that we must play our part in developing the country, and so our mantra is ‘Building tourism for all Jamaicans’, and that includes entertainment,” he said.

Greatness Weekend, now in its second staging, will be held under the theme ‘I Choose Kingston’ and will bring together four events across the Corporate Area.

The festivities begin on October 16 with Pool Cooler Fete (PCF), followed by RECALL: Throwback Festival on October 17. Both events will celebrate their 10th anniversaries this year.

CUPS: Château Blanc follows on October 18 before the weekend culminates with the Greatness Pink & White Brunch on October 19.

Promoters representing the events were on hand for Tuesday’s launch which also welcomed mayor of Kingston, Councillor Andrew Swaby.

Mikisha Silvera, destination manager for Kingston and St Andrew at the Tourism Product Development Company Limited (TPDCo), lauded the promoters for their contribution to Kingston’s entertainment landscape, and said Greatness Weekend could further strengthen the capital’s appeal as a destination.

“When you look at what they have done so far, it’s amazing. Kingston is the cultural mecca of Jamaica. We’re talking about nightlife, daylife, gastronomy. The culture that exists here is a rich cultural heritage,” Silvera said.

She noted that the weekend provides an opportunity for Jamaicans and international visitors alike to experience the capital’s cultural offerings.

“We’re able to participate as citizens, as well as the visitors who will be coming here for Greatness Weekend. The brand being here is something special, and you’re going to be a part of Jamaica’s history,” she said.

Silvera said initiatives such as Greatness Weekend can help position Kingston as a premier destination by combining entertainment, culture, food, and tourism into a single experience.

The packed launch offered guests a taste of the festivities to come, with specially prepared rum mixes sponsored by Rich Rum adding to the evening’s celebratory atmosphere.

World.title: ‘It a mash wi up’
World.content:
Nicole Watson returns a cellphone that was left with her by a customer, shortly after she exited the embassy. Photos: Naphtali Junior

AT least two Kingston entrepreneurs whose livelihoods depend on charging US Embassy visitors a fee to store their mobile devices or provide them with phone calls are requesting a meeting with embassy officials, seeking ways to adapt after a new policy permitting applicants to bring cellphones inside the facility.

The applicants themselves have expressed mixed views about the policy change, with some welcoming the move, rejoicing that they no longer have to pay people outside the embassy to keep their devices while inside, and others expressing scepticism.

Cellphones are just one of the many items now permitted within the walls of the US Embassy. In an advisory on September 1 the embassy said small quantities of baby formula, baby food, milk, diapers, and baby carriers that can pass through an X-ray machine are now permitted. Other items include money, belts, watches, keys, earbuds, medical devices, and non-liquid medication, which must be declared before security screening.

Prohibited items include computers, intelligent eyewear, and other electronic devices, inclusive of media devices, such as compact discs (CDs), thumb drives, memory cards, flash drives, headphones, and speakers. Additionally, cameras or video equipment, flashlights, lighters and matches, weapons, knives, and other sharp objects are not allowed. Alcoholic beverages, purses larger than 18 inches, liquids, lotions, oils, and gels are also not allowed inside.

But for Nicole Watson, a vendor who, for more than 15 years, has made a living holding on to cellphones for visa applicants, the move to allow previously banned cellphones is most troubling.

“It’s something that we all live off [of]. I don’t know what transpired; it’s odd. We are out here to help each and every one. You have good, and you have bad, but we would just like the embassy to look over things or draw us in a meeting because this is our daily bread. If there are bad apples out here that they need to talk to, they can talk to them to keep the things flowing because we have kids to go to school,” she told the Jamaica Observer, lamenting the cost of living.

Watson said the change has destroyed her business.

“It a mash we up; it crush up, it gone,” she bemoaned.

“I normally have around four buses that come to me in the morning time from May Pen, Mandeville, Savanna-la-Mar, and Montego Bay. I reach here like five in the morning time, or if them call me four o’clock, I will reach down. If possible, I would get 30 people for the day, because I’m known down here, so people just come… On a good day, about 500 or 600 persons come to them [at the embassy], so I can get at least 35 people. Now, everybody passes,” she said.

Watson shared that she typically charges $1,000 to store cellphones, $300 for phone calls, and $500 for WhatsApp phone calls, money she said added up to support her and her children, but now she is barely making ends meet.

“It’s hard because the sun is hot and business is slow,” she said.

A look around the area outside the embassy proved her words to be true, as many other runners sat in the sun along the side of the road across from the embassy, eagerly awaiting business that never came.

Watson had just two phones in her bag; she said she got them from loyal customers who still support her business.

“Because I am out here long time, I will have my clients who come and I will say, ‘Alright, just give me a lunch money and gwaan,’ but from people hear what is going on now they just move along. We nuh bother press anybody; we just make them move along,” she told the Sunday Observer.

Despite slow business, Watson said she will not leave the area. Instead, she will continue to sell phone cards and beverages.

“Food have to eat, and gas have to buy. Me nah go do no nine-to-five work because me nah work for $17,000 a week. I cyaan bother with that because that can’t buy gas put in car,” she reasoned.

Another vendor, who chose to remain anonymous, expressed concern that she would not be able to take care of her children.

“My son inna 10 grade and my daughter inna eight grade, and it’s this send them go [to] school… I start it from them in basic school, then primary school, and now high school… I don’t know how me a go manage,” she said.

“A me alone a take care of them, no father, no nothing. Me nuh have no help,” she bemoaned.

“It mash up. If we can talk to them and bring it back, that would be good, but I don’t think talking a go bring it back either. We just have to have in our mind what else we are going to do after,” she said.

Outside the embassy, applicants and family members sat patiently, awaiting their appointment. For some, the move to allow cellphones was welcomed, but one man was sceptical.

“When I came here last week and I heard about it, I told the person, ‘Don’t take your phone inside there’, ” he said, adding that he planned to leave his phone in his car.

However, for a woman who gave her name as Jennifer, she loved the idea of not having to stress about where she would store her cellphone.

“The first time I came here I had to pay somebody to keep my phone outside, so it’s a good idea. At the time, I did not know that I could not bring in lotion and stuff in my bag, so when I got here I had to throw away things, so it’s good. At least we don’t have to pay money out here now because sometimes they charge $1,500 to hold the phone, and that can buy credit. It’s a good move,” she told the Sunday Observer.

World.title: ULTIMATE PUSH
World.content:
Jamaica’s Rushell Clayton will be in action in the women’s 400m hurldes final at the World Athletics Ultimate Championships in Budapest, Hungary, today.AFP

JAMAICA came up short on the second day of the inaugural World Athletics Ultimate Championships at the National Athletics Center in Budapest, Hungary, with Oblique Seville’s second-place finish in the men’s 100m the best result on Saturday.

Jamaicans contested four finals, including the men’s 100m, women’s 100m, women’s 400m and men’s long jump, and will be looking for better results on Sunday, the third and final day.

Commonwealth Games champion Sanique Walker and two-time World Athletics Championships bronze medallist Rushell Clayton have qualified for the final of the women’s 400m hurdles.

They will join Romaine Beckford, who is in the men’s high jump; Ackelia Smith, who is in the women’s triple jump; and the mixed 4x400m relay team.

Additionally, Jamaica will hope to get into the 200m finals, with Bryan Levell and Christopher Taylor in the men’s semi-finals and Ashanti Moore and Lavanya Williams in the women’s semi-finals.

Seville, the World champion and Diamond League winner, was upstaged by American Kenny Bednarek who won the final in a season’s best 9.85 seconds (-0.6m/s). Seville repeated the 9.90 seconds he ran to lead the semi-finals but was edged on the finishing line.

Another American, Ronnie Baker, was third in 9.93 seconds.

Seville had easily won his semi-final while Ackeem Blake failed to get past the semi-finals after running 10.21 seconds.

Jonielle Smith was the best-placed Jamaican in a quality women’s 100m final, placing fourth in 10.94 seconds (-0.2m/s), the same time recorded by her compatriot Tina Clayton, while Lavanya Williams was seventh in 11.07 seconds.

American Melissa Jefferson-Wooden ran a world-leading 10.62 seconds to win the title, just beating Julien Alfred of St Lucia, 10.74 seconds, with Sha’Carri Richardson of the USA third in 10.76 seconds.

Jodean Williams had run 11.16 seconds for fifth in her semi-final while Brianna Lyston had run 11.18 seconds in her first race.

National record holder Nickisha Pryce was third in the women’s 400m final, running 49.56 seconds as favourite Marileidy Paulino of the Dominican Republic won in 49.07 seconds, coming from fourth place over the last 120 metres to take the title.

Norway’s Henriette Jaeger was second in 49.28 seconds.

In the other final that included a Jamaican, Diamond League winner Tajay Gayle was fifth in the men’s long jump with a best of 7.90m (-0.1m/s), after failing to make the top four for the fourth and final round.

Gayle improved with each jump, starting with 7.52m (1.0m/s) and then had a 7.72m (-0.2m/s) jump in the second round.

Walker lowered the 54.00 seconds she ran to win the Commonwealth Games, improving her personal best to 53.77 seconds as she placed third in her semi-final from lane nine behind Americans Jasmine Jones, who ran a season’s best 52.77 seconds, and Anna Cockrell, who ran 53.31 seconds.

Clayton was fourth in her semi-final in 53.84 seconds, after she came off the seventh hurdle in seventh place.

Emma Zapletalova of Slovakia won her semi-final in 52.93 seconds, followed by Panama’s Gianna Woodruff, 53.73 seconds, and Belgium’s national record holder Paulien Couckuyt, 53.81 seconds.

Commonwealth Games champion Navasky Anderson just missed out on a place in the men’s 800m final, finishing fifth in the first semi-final in 1:44.83 behind Kenya’s Emmanuel Wanyonyi who was fourth in 1:44.43 to secure a place in the final.

World.title: THE CLOTH @ Harrods
World.content:
LOOK 04 — Curepe Top (Courtesy of Brand63Africa)

First…



Caribbean cool meets Knightsbridge…

The Harrods x Brand63Africa pop-up has officially landed on the fifth floor of the iconic London flagship, spotlighting five standout design houses: Christie Brown, Studio Namnyak, Abiola Olusola, Sukeina and Trinidad & Tobago’s very own The Cloth.

The only Caribbean label in the edit, The Cloth joins four African brands in a stylish showcase curated by Brand63Africa founder Eva Omaghomi — moving emerging talent from niche discovery to the luxury main floor.

Consider this your sign to put African and Caribbean design on the Harrods itinerary. SO2 applauds Sophie Bufton and Robert Young.

Harrods, Knightsbridge

September 7 – October 27

From The Cloth

“It’s the one I love!”

A rather special reaction from Edward Enninful, former editor-in-chief of British Vogue and founder of EE72, on seeing The Cloth’s Mauby in tartan from our AW26–27 collection.

World.title: Shabba Ranks files lawsuit against publishing arm of Greensleeves Records
World.content:
Shabba Ranks

Iconic dancehall trailblazer and deejay, Shabba Ranks, has filed a lawsuit against the publishing arm of Greensleeves Records, in a move to reclaim the rights to several of his crossover hits as well as the 1990 song Dem Bow.

According to a report in Billboard magazine, Shabba Ranks (born Rexton Gordon) filed the suit on Friday (Sept. 11), and it aims to reclaim compositions including the Billboard Hot 100 hits Slow and Sexy, Housecall, Mr Loverman and Let’s Get It On.

Shabba Ranks’ catalogue also includes the 1990 song Dem Bow, the namesake for reggaetón’s iconic dembow rhythm that is currently at the centre of a long-running copyright infringement lawsuit entangling the entire genre.

Friday’s lawsuit, meanwhile, centres on copyright termination — the provision of United States (US) copyright law that enables authors to claw back their intellectual property decades after signing it away.

Shabba Ranks first notified Greensleeves in 2023 that he wanted to exercise his termination right, but the publisher said no. According to Greensleeves, his 1989 publishing deal stipulated that his compositions were “works made for hire,” which are explicitly excluded from the copyright termination statute.

Shabba, however, is contesting the validity of that work-for-hire provision, and he wants a judge to declare that his copyright termination is effective regardless.

“The compositions are not and could not have been works made for hire under the US Copyright Act, regardless of the language of the assignment,” wrote Shabba Ranks’ attorneys at Reitler Kailas & Rosenblatt.

“Gordon was never at any time an employee of [Greensleeves], and musical compositions are not recognised in the US Copyright Act as a type of work that can be deemed a work made for hire simply by agreement between the hiring party and a non-employee author.”

Copyright termination is a hot topic in music law in the United States at present.

Pioneering rap outfit Salt-N-Pepa is battling Universal Music Group (UMG) over the provision in a case that has caught the industry’s attention.

Meanwhile, all three major labels are currently trying to get the Supreme Court to reverse a controversial recent ruling that extended the termination right overseas.

Shabba Ranks, raised in Seaview Gardens, rode high in the late 1980s into the mid-1990s with a steady streak of hit songs. He signed with Epic Records and scored back-to-back wins at the Grammy Awards when As Raw As Ever and X-tra Naked won the Best Reggae Album awards in 1992 and 1993, respectively.

Both albums have been certified gold by the Recording Industry Association of America.

World.title: France climbs down in social media row with U.S. after ambassador’s appointment blocked
World.content:
AFP reported that the U.S. State Department responded positively to the apology. “We take note of France’s statement and appreciate it; we look forward to collaborating with them to promote our common values ​​and interests,” a State Department official told AFP on condition of anonymity.

The appointment of French diplomat Aurélien Lechevallier as ambassador to the U.S. was blocked by Washington as a result of the spat, France24 reports.

The dispute began in July when the French mission to the U.N. in Geneva posted on X that “The U.S. used to be a beacon of human rights. Not anymore.” This comment came after the U.S. voted against renewing the term of the UN Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk.

Two days later after the French mission’s social media post, the U.S. walked out of a U.N. security council meeting when France’s representative began to speak.

The apology from France and acceptance from the U.S. paves the way for Lechevallier to be confirmed for the Washington role. Currently chief of staff to French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot, Lechevallier is set to replace Laurent Bili as France’s U.S. envoy.

It’s not the first time the two countries have had a diplomatic spat. Last year, France summoned U.S. Ambassador Charles Kushner after he published an open letter accusing President Emmanuel Macron’s government of not doing enough to combat rising antisemitism in his country.

World.title: Russian drone hits passenger train headed from Kyiv to Warsaw
World.content:
Ukraine's Foreign Affairs Minister Andrii Sybiha said that Russian President Vladimir Putin’s forces are “knocking directly on the doors of the EU and NATO.” | Genya Savilov/AFP via Getty Images

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha responded to the attack by stating that Russian President Vladimir Putin’s forces are “knocking directly on the doors of the EU and NATO.”

BRUSSELS — Russian drones attacked a crossing point on the Polish-Ukrainian border on Sunday morning, hitting a passenger train two kilometers from the frontier in Volyn Oblast.

Ukraine’s state rail operator confirmed that a strike hit the locomotive of a passenger train bound for Warsaw. The train crew were warned of the threat in advance by Ukrainian authorities and no one was injured, the operator added.

Separately, social media videos showed a large fire at a gas station near the Yahodyn–Dorohusk crossing point between Ukraine and Poland. According to local media, there are no reports yet of casualties from the gas station fire.

World.title: How to watch Sweden’s election like a pro
World.content:
That means there are only two realistic candidates to be prime minister: the incumbent, conservative Moderate party leader Ulf Kristersson; and Magdalena Andersson, the former PM who leads Sweden’s biggest party, the center-left Social Democrats.

Swedish Prime Minister and Moderate Party leader Ulf Kristersson speaks to the media upon arrival to a televised election debate hosted by TV4 in Stockholm, Sweden, on September 10, 2026, three days ahead of the country’s general election. | Jonathan Nackstrand/ AFP via Getty Images

Kristersson has run the right-wing coalition for the past four years thanks to influential support from the second biggest party, the far-right Sweden Democrats. They backed him in votes in parliament and drove policy in a hardline direction, including crackdowns on crime and especially immigration. But the Sweden Democrats did not join the coalition cabinet. That could now change.

Can the far right enter the government?

Kristersson divided opinion in 2022 when he broke a decades-long taboo against working with the far right and did his deal with the Sweden Democrats, who had won 20% of the vote. The SD was founded in the 1980s and some members in those days had roots in neo-Nazi movements. The party has taken steps to clean up its act in recent years, though not to everyone’s satisfaction.

Now Kristersson says he will give the SD ministerial seats in government if his side wins on Sunday, as part of an agreement with the far-right leader, Jimmie Åkesson. That would be another huge step for Sweden and one that the opposition has seized on.

“Of course this would be a different country with a government with half of the ministers from the Sweden Democrats,” opposition leader Andersson told AP recently. “It would not be good for Sweden if they would get the keys to the ministry of defense or the ministry of foreign affairs.”

Kristersson insists he would still be in charge overall. He points to his work with Åkesson over the past four years which he says has revived the economy and cut rates of violent crime and immigration, both of which had been major public concerns. “I can guarantee you that it will only be very skilled and experienced and people with good judgment that would be part of my government,” he told POLITICO.

World.title: Will Lagarde bite the apple? ECB president leaves everyone guessing in Normandy
World.content:
On stage, she even encouraged reporters who made the trip to Normandy to cover her potential political comeback to pack up early, promising that they would be disappointed.

But there are signs suggesting that the ECB chief, who entered into politics during the presidency of France's apple-loving Jacques Chirac, is increasingly willing to weigh in on the campaign.

While she promised to stay at least until the end of the year, Lagarde previously refused to rule out leaving before the end of her term, which ends in October 2027.

Earlier this week, she announced that she would publish her first autobiography, Lady First, in January. She also waded into the French presidential debate by rejecting French far-left presidential contender Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s proposal to wipe out government debt.

Her presence at the apple festival in the 15th-century Manoir de la Fortière — an unconventional locale for a central banker's speech — might be yet another signal. Opening the event, Morin said that he tried to invite her for years but never managed to make it work. Until this year.

Christine Lagarde at the Fête de la Pomme, France, on September 12, 202. | Giorgio Leali/POLITICO

“Everyone is happy to have you here and I realized to what extent you have an exceptional reputation,” said Morin, who worked with Lagarde when they both served as ministers under conservative president Nicolas Sarkozy, including during the 2008 financial crisis.

World.title: EU-Parlament öffnet sich für härtere China-Politik
World.content:
Brüssel und Peking führen derzeit Verhandlungen darüber, wie das Handelsdefizit der EU gegenüber China in Höhe von 1 Milliarde Euro pro Tag ausgeglichen werden kann. Ein Anstieg der chinesischen Exporte hat die einheimischen Hersteller unter Druck gesetzt und Schrecken geschürt, dass der Kontinent angesichts vielbeachteter Werksschließungen in der Automobil- und Chemieindustrie eine Deindustrialisierung durchläuft.

EU-Handelskommissar Maroš Šefčovič wird im Oktober im Rahmen der Gespräche nach Peking reisen. Er erklärte, die Union sei bereit zu handeln, falls bis zu diesem Zeitpunkt keine Fortschritte erzielt würden.

Die Kommission erwägt Maßnahmen, um Chinas industrieller Dominanz entgegenzuwirken, darunter neue Vorschriften, die Unternehmen dazu anregen sollen, ihre kritischen Lieferketten zu diversifizieren, sowie Schutzmaßnahmen, die die Einfuhr wichtiger Güter wie Hybrid-Elektrofahrzeuge begrenzen würden.

In einer gemeinsamen Erklärung vom Donnerstag sprach sich der Ausschuss für auswärtige Angelegenheiten des Europäischen Parlaments für eine Eindämmung der chinesischen Exporte und der übermäßigen Abhängigkeit Europas von Rohstoffen bis hin zu Halbleitern aus und forderte die EU auf, Maßnahmen zu ergreifen, um die „Instrumentalisierung der wirtschaftlichen Abhängigkeit der EU“ einzudämmen.

„Business as usual“ gibt es nicht mehr

Canfin erklärte, unter den EU-Abgeordneten setze sich zunehmend die Erkenntnis durch, dass „Business as usual“ in den Beziehungen der Union zu Peking keine Option mehr sei. Als Beleg für den Wandel in der Haltung gegenüber China verwies er auf die wachsende Unterstützung im Parlament für eine offensivere Industriepolitik.

Die Abgeordneten arbeiten derzeit an ihrer Position zum vorgeschlagenen „Industrial Accelerator Act“, mit dem im Rahmen der umweltorientierten öffentlichen Beschaffung eine europäische Präferenz in strategischen Industriezweigen verankert werden soll. Die federführenden Abgeordneten dieses wegweisenden Gesetzentwurfs streben einen eng verbundenen „Made in Europe“-Club sowie eine strengere Prüfung ausländischer Direktinvestitionen an.

World.title: Trump says he would ‘love’ to see a united Ireland
World.content:
Donald Trump and Taoiseach Micheál Martin listen to a question from the media at Farmleigh House in Phoenix Park in the Irish capital Dublin on September 12, 2026. | Brendan Smialowski/AFP via Getty Images

“It’s going to happen eventually,” the U.S. president said in Dublin during a golf-focused trip to the long-divided island.

DUBLIN — U.S. President Donald Trump waded into another age-old conflict Saturday, declaring on a golf-focused visit to Ireland that he’d like to see the island unified — the nightmare scenario for Northern Ireland’s British unionists.

Sitting beside Irish Taoiseach Micheál Martin after an overnight flight from Washington, Trump said he couldn’t understand why Northern Ireland — the part of the island that remained in the U.K. when the rest of Ireland won independence over a century ago — hadn’t already joined the Republic of Ireland.

“I’d love to see it unified. I think it’d be great. A great feather in everybody’s cap if that happened. It’s going to happen eventually,” Trump said, gesturing to Martin, who has spent years trying behind the scenes to build better relations with unionists, to little avail. “You’ve got the right man over here to get it moving. But I think it would be a fantastic thing. Now the U.K. will have something to say about it obviously. But I think it’d be a great thing. How can it be bad?”

World.title: Farage’s Reform UK gets two £36M donations from crypto billionaires
World.content:
Delo argued in an opinion piece for The Telegraph that Reform needed the injection to make the election “a fair fight.” Delo, who was already one of Reform’s largest donors, said he wanted to give Reform “a level playing field” at the next general election.

The paper on Saturday also published an opinion piece from Harborne, where he called his donation “a philantropic gift to our country.”

Farage thanked the two men for their contributions. “Both men know that we are the only party that can turn the country around,” he said in a statement.

Reform UK was leading the polls since April 2025 , according to POLITICO’s Poll of Polls. But the party has now slumped slightly behind Labour, with new Prime Minister Andy Burnham at the helm and after a bizarre by-election where Farage defeated satirical candidate Count Binface.

The right-wing force is currently rushing to get battle-ready amid speculation Burnham could trigger an early general election, though one is not due until 2029. Reform UK is on the hunt for potential candidates to run as MP, and has only about 100 star candidates considered ready to run at the moment.

World.title: Portugal wants EU cash to pay for firefighting goats
World.content:
José Manuel Fernandes Minister of Agriculture and Fisheries of Portugal at the European Council in Brussels in Belgium on 9 December 2024. | Martin Bertrand/Hans Lucas/AFP via Getty Images

As budget negotiations intensify, capitals are reaching for a new argument to keep money in the farming pot: climate change.

Portugal’s minister for agriculture has a burning desire for the next EU long-term budget: more goats.

José Manuel Fernandes wants Brussels to help pay shepherds to let goats, cows and sheep graze on shrubs in areas at high risk of wildfires — a low-tech approach that experts say the EU has been ignoring for too long. Portugal and some regions in Spain are already running their own programs.

“We are using our national money, but it is work that we are doing for all the European Union,” Fernandes told POLITICO at an informal meeting of ministers in Dublin, arguing that preventing fires helps lower carbon emissions.

World.title: Austria's new headscarf ban for under-14s sparks debate over religious freedom
World.content:
Since the start of the 2026/27 school year on 1 September, female pupils in Austria under the age of 14 have been prohibited from wearing any headscarf at school that "covers the head in line with Islamic traditions."

 

Teachers' representatives say the new rule has generally been implemented calmly and respectfully. At the same time, some schools have reported conflicts and, in some cases, aggressive reactions.

The new law was already controversial before it came into force, with critics questioning whether it was compatible with freedom of religion and the principle of equality.

In 2020, Austria's Constitutional Court (VfGH) overturned an earlier headscarf ban. That law had prohibited primary school pupils from wearing religious or ideologically motivated clothing that covered the head and applied to children until the end of the school year in which they turned 10.

However, the VfGH found that the rule violated the principle of equality and freedom of religion. In the court's view, the law in practice was primarily aimed at the "Islamic" headscarf.

An international issue: women protest in Lahore on 13 February 2022 against a headscarf ban for Muslim schoolgirls in neighbouring India. AP Photo

The new law differs in its higher age limit.

The government says the main goal is to protect children's development and their freedom to develop as individuals, arguing that girls should be protected from potential family or social pressure to wear a headscarf.

The VfGH has not yet ruled on whether this revised justification, and the new design of the ban, address the constitutional concerns raised previously.

Teachers required to enforce ban

For the time being, schools and teachers are responsible for putting the ban into practice.

If a teacher notices that a pupil is wearing such a headscarf despite the ban, they are required to ask the pupil to remove it as a first step. If the pupil refuses, further discussions will take place. If necessary, the education authority may be brought in. Only at later stages can administrative penalty proceedings be initiated.

Students who repeatedly violate the ban can expect to face a multi-stage process, and parents or guardians could be fined between €150 and €800 if the headscarf continues to be worn despite being asked to remove it.

Representatives of the teachers' union have criticised the obligation on teachers to report breaches and warned that it risks putting them in a monitoring role that goes beyond their educational work.

Reports of threats and refusal to attend school

Possible threats and refusal to attend school have also become part of the debate surrounding the new law.

Austria's government had, even before the law was passed, pointed to cases in which girls or women were put under pressure both to wear and to remove a headscarf.

Integration Minister Claudia Plakolm referred, among other things, to instances of threats within families.

There are currently no statistics that would show how often such situations arise in Austrian schools.

Reports of pupils who do not attend lessons at all or do so only irregularly because of the headscarf ban also still need to be properly assessed. There are indications of isolated cases of refusal and conflict.

Women hold up a banner reading: AP Photo

Supporters of the new rules argue that girls at this age are particularly dependent on their families and could therefore be exposed to considerable social or religious pressure.

Critics have countered these concerns by questioning whether a state ban really strengthens the self-determination of the pupils concerned. A girl who wishes to wear a headscarf "of her own conviction" can no longer follow through with that decision at school because of the ban.

People protest in Rome on 1 October 2022 over the death of Mahsa Amin (22), who died in police custody in Iran. She had allegedly worn her head covering too loosely. AP Photo

There are also concerns from education experts. Psychologist Christiane Spiel warned on ORF of potential loyalty conflicts for children if parents insist on wearing a headscarf while the school demands that it be removed.

New constitutional challenge is pending

Before the law came into force, several parents had already tried to challenge it directly before the VfGH.

The court rejected these applications on formal grounds, as those concerned had not yet been directly affected by the law at that point.

A new application for the law to be struck down has now been filed.

The key issue, once again, is likely to be the relationship between freedom of religion and the principle of equality.

Among other things, the court will have to examine whether protecting children from religious or family pressure justifies an "interference with freedom of religion" and whether a general headscarf ban is necessary and proportionate to achieve this.

World.title: Russian drone hits train two km from Polish border, rail operator says
World.content:
A Russian drone struck the locomotive of a passenger train two kilometres from the Polish border on Sunday, Ukraine's state-owned rail operator Ukrzaliznytsia (Ukrainian Railways) said.

 

The attack reportedly took place in Ukraine's Volyn region. There are not believed to have been any casualties from the incident.

"For the second day in a row, the enemy has been attacking the railways. Today in the Volyn region, two km from the border with Poland, the enemy struck the locomotive of a passenger train," Ukrzaliznytsia said on Telegram.

A tragedy was apparently averted thanks in part to an early warning. The team responsible for monitoring threats to the rail service detected the danger and alerted the train crew in good time, allowing them time to take measures to protect passengers and staff, per the company.

"We are continuing to monitor aerial threats, ensure the smooth running of trains and take every possible measure to ensure the safety of passengers and railway staff," it added.

The strike near the Polish border came as part of a broader Russian air offensive.

According to the Ukrainian Air Force, Russia launched more than 450 drones at Ukraine overnight, including jet-propelled drones and Banderol missile drones.

At least three people were killed and 36 people were injured in the overnight strikes.

Russian attacks also hit regions of western Ukraine bordering Poland.

The scale of the attacks meant that traffic at Polish–Ukrainian border crossings had to be temporarily restricted. Border Guard spokesperson Major Dariusz Sienicki told the PAP news agency that checks had been suspended overnight for safety reasons.

Border traffic has now returned to normal at Dorohusk, Zosin and Dołhobyczów. Processing at Hrebenne was also expected to resume.

The Border Guard did not record any direct threat at Polish crossings.

"We only received information from the Ukrainian side that a drone struck and destroyed a lorry at a distance of about 800 metres from the Jagodzin crossing," Major Sienicki said.

Former British Prime Minister Boris Johnson and Günter Sautter - a close adviser to German Chancellor Friedrich Merz - were among a number of political figures and diplomats on board a train that stopped and was partially evacuated while heading from Kyiv to Poland amid drone warnings on Sunday morning, German outlet Der Spiegel reported.

Russia 'knocking at the doors of the EU and NATO'

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said the "barbaric Russian strikes" were "not just a continuation of its attacks on our state borders."

"This is Putin’s terror 'knocking' directly on the doors of the EU and NATO. Russian barbarians are at your gate, dear partners," he wrote on X, while also calling for further sanctions against Moscow.

"Make Moscow feel the consequences of its terror. Not just half-decisions, but uncompromising, powerful steps. Full trade embargo. Full entry bans. Full sanctions on the military-industrial complex," he urged.

Poland scrambled military aircraft

In response to the Russian attacks on western Ukraine, the Polish armed forces took steps to secure the country's airspace, with the deployment of Polish aircraft and other preventive measures.

Residents of the Lublin and Podkarpackie regions received a morning alert from the Government Centre for Security warning of a Russian air attack on Ukrainian territory and informing them about the activity of Polish military aircraft. The alert was cancelled at around 9 am, after roughly five hours.

Shortly before 10 am, the Operational Command of the Armed Forces announced that military aircraft were no longer operating in Polish airspace. It stressed at the same time that Poland's airspace had not been violated.

Poland's defence minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, said Polish defence systems had detected an early-morning attack using Geran-5 drones in western Ukraine.

"One of them struck 1 km from the border with Poland, another 5 km. The Polish airspace was guarded by F16 aircraft, helicopters, and the SAAB airborne reconnaissance aircraft. There was no breach of our border," he said.
